top_pain_points.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocking issue: the kanban dashboard task creation path consistently fails to trigger the automation chain (plan→code→revision), which is the core value proposition of the tool. The error 'failed after 3 attempts' indicates the retry mechanism was exhausted, confirming a persistent failure rather than a transient glitch. Multiple comments on the issue suggest other users are encountering the same problem. The generic error message ('last error: error') also represents a poor debugging experience, hiding the root cause from users. Labeled as 'bug' by maintainers, reinforcing the validity of the complaint.

source_issues.title: GenerativeModelStore: _last_fetch_id can regress and defeat incremental fetch
source_issues.evidence: _last_fetch_id is updated to the max id of the delta batch on each poll, not a monotonic high-water mark. When an incremental fetch returns rows whose max id is lower than the previously-seen max, the cursor regresses and the next poll re-fetches everything between the new (smaller) cursor and the true global max, defeating the daemon's egress-savings purpose and causing unnecessary DB reads in cloud environments.

source_issues.title: Security: rendis/opcode exposes unauthenticated MCP/SSE endpoint on :4100 with auto-registered agents and built-in shell.exec, enabling remote code execution
source_issues.evidence: rendis/opcode MCP/SSE daemon installs via 'opcode install --listen' and binds to all interfaces without auth. The exposed endpoint auto-registers agents and exposes a built-in shell.exec tool callable by any network caller. Direct RCE vector: no user interaction, no credential, no confirmation required. Any local user or network peer who can reach :4100 gains OS command execution under the host user's authority.

source_issues.title: Security: sadikjarvis/native-run forwards chat messages into subprocess shell=True on the local host, enabling chat-to-shell command execution
source_issues.evidence: sadikjarvis/native-run bridges OpenClaw chat input directly to subprocess shell=True on the local host. Any chat message accepted by the agent triggers shell command execution under the local user's authority. This bypasses all OpenClaw safety controls: the agent treats user text as natural language, but the plugin converts it to shell commands. Attackers can craft chat messages to execute arbitrary commands (file exfiltration, credential theft, persistence). No secondary exploitation chain needed.

top_pain_points.topic: Session I/O wrappers silently swallow DB exceptions and return None, causing permanent chat history loss
top_pain_points.summary: In _storage.py, read/write session wrapper functions catch all exceptions and return None instead of re-raising. When a transient DB failure occurs, callers cannot distinguish it from 'session not found', so they create a fresh empty AgentSession — permanently discarding all prior chat history. This is a silent data loss bug that provides no error signal to users.

signals.topic: GenerativeModelStore incremental fetch cursor regression causing unnecessary DB re-fetches in cloud environments
signals.summary: _last_fetch_id is updated to the max ID of each delta batch rather than a monotonic high-water mark. When a lower-ID model is updated, the cursor regresses, causing the next poll to re-fetch the entire range between the regressed cursor and the true max, silently defeating the daemon's DB egress reduction purpose and inflating cloud costs.
signals.review_reason: Functional bug with direct cost implications for cloud users. The incremental fetch daemon is designed to minimize DB egress; the cursor regression silently causes full-range re-fetches on every poll cycle where a low-ID model is updated, defeating the stated cost-reduction purpose. Bug is labeled 'bug', confirmed by code-level analysis with reproduction walkthrough. Count=1, single repo, so P1 not P0.

source_issues.title: GenerativeModelStore: _last_fetch_id can regress and defeat incremental fetch
source_issues.evidence: _last_fetch_id is updated to the max id of the delta batch on each poll, not a monotonic high-water mark. When an incremental fetch returns rows whose max id is lower than the previously-seen max, the cursor regresses and the next poll re-fetches everything between the new (smaller) cursor and the true global max, defeating the daemon's egress-savings purpose and causing unnecessary DB reads in cloud environments.

signals.topic: Path Traversal vulnerability in EmailToolKit attachment download
signals.summary: The EmailToolKit's `download_attachment` function does not validate the filename obtained from `part.get_filename()`, allowing an attacker to craft a malicious attachment filename (e.g., '../hack.py') to write files outside the intended directory. A proof-of-concept demonstrates writing files to arbitrary paths, which could lead to remote code execution in containerized environments.
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1 且无用户实际被利用的报告，但该路径穿越漏洞具有明确的 POC 验证：攻击者可利用邮件附件文件名写入任意路径，在容器化部署环境下可直接导致 RCE。用户若使用 EmailToolKit 读取含恶意附件的邮件即可能被攻击。该漏洞影响关键安全边界（文件系统隔离），reviewer 已确认为 Security 标签，属于真实可利用的安全缺陷而非仅理论风险。综合判断为 P1 而非 P0，因缺少用户被实际影响的多条证据。

source_issues.title: [Security] Path Traversal in EmailToolKit
source_issues.evidence: POC demonstrates attachment with filename='../hack.py' writes to /app/hack.py outside the intended Test1 directory, confirming arbitrary file write via path traversal. No evidence of active exploitation or user-reported incidents.
