signals.review_reason: 体验退化问题：长对话后 /new 命令延迟明显（1-3秒 vs 原版 100-300ms），虽非阻断但显著影响高频用户的使用流畅度，有具体性能对比数据

source_issues.title: [Performance] /new 命令响应慢，长对话后延迟明显
source_issues.evidence: 延迟可能来自 Zustand 状态重置全量重渲染、Electron IPC 多跳通信、DOM 节点无虚拟滚动等问题，与原版 OpenClaw 流畅度差距明显

signals.topic: Formatter layer causes memory leak, API 400 rejections, and crashes during long conversations
signals.summary: Multiple critical bugs in formatter classes (TruncatedFormatterBase, DeepSeekChatFormatter, OpenAIChatFormatter) combine to cause unbounded memory growth, API rejection cascades, and Python OOM crashes in long-running agent conversations. Root causes: (A) deepcopy(msgs) on every API call doubles memory per request; (B) null content field causes API 400 rejections; (C) None tool output causes TypeError crashes.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed, multi-faceted critical bug causing real user impact: Python OOM crashes, API 400 rejection cascades, and an infinite crash loop during long conversations. The issue has detailed reproduction steps, concrete error messages, and root cause analysis. It blocks the main workflow (ReActAgent with tools) for users running extended conversations.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Formatter memory leak and content:null API rejection cascade
source_issues.evidence: Memory grows from ~200MB to 3GB+ over long conversations; Python OOM crashes; API returns 400 Bad Request for null content; infinite crash loop when combined with session replay

signals.topic: ReActAgent exits loop prematurely when LLM returns only thinking blocks (empty response bug)
signals.summary: The ReActAgent loop's exit condition only checks for absence of tool_use blocks, but does not verify presence of text content. When using models with extended thinking (Claude, Qwen with thinking enabled), the LLM may return only thinking blocks with no text and no tool_use, causing the agent to break and return an effectively empty response to the user.
aliases: thinking-only LLM response causes empty reply
agent loop breaks on thinking blocks
signals.review_reason: A confirmed main-workflow bug that causes the ReActAgent to silently produce empty responses to users when using thinking-capable models. This directly blocks the primary use case (reasoning-acting agent loop) and produces silent failures (no error message) that are hard for users to diagnose.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ReActAgent exits loop prematurely when LLM returns only thinking blocks (no text, no tool_use)
source_issues.evidence: Agent returns msg_reasoning with only thinking blocks and no user-visible text content, effectively producing an empty response. Confirmed with Claude thinking-enabled and Qwen thinking-enabled models.

signals.topic: Studio (agentscope web UI) npm global installation fails
signals.summary: Users are unable to install the agentscope studio web UI via npm install -g @agentscope/studio. Multiple attempts fail with errors, blocking access to the graphical debugging/development interface.
signals.review_reason: Installation failure blocks the studio web UI entirely, which is a key developer-facing feature for debugging and visualization. Multiple retry attempts by the user failed, indicating a persistent installation barrier.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 有谁成功安装studio吗？npm install -g @agentscope/studio安装失败，各种尝试都不行
source_issues.evidence: npm install -g @agentscope/studio fails with errors across multiple attempts. Screenshots of installation failure errors provided.

signals.topic: tool_choice parameter unsupported on many model providers
signals.summary: The tool_choice parameter causes 'unsupported' errors across many model providers when using the agentscope wrapper. Users are unable to use tool_choice functionality, which is a key feature for controlling tool selection behavior.
signals.review_reason: tool_choice is a core parameter for controlling LLM tool selection behavior. When it fails across multiple models, it blocks the key workflow of tool-use agents. The bug is confirmed with error screenshots.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: tool_choice参数支持的问题
source_issues.evidence: tool_choice parameter throws unsupported errors on multiple models. Screenshot of error from model API provided.

signals.topic: OpenAIChatModel.__call__ missing response parameters (finish_reason, tool_calls, function_call)
signals.summary: The OpenAIChatModel wrapper omits several parameters that the native OpenAI SDK returns, including finish_reason, tool_calls, function_call, and reasoning/thinking content. This breaks upstream code that depends on these fields.
signals.review_reason: Missing API response fields breaks downstream code that depends on them (e.g., finish_reason for controlling loop logic, tool_calls for tool execution). While only 1 issue reported, the impact on any code using these standard fields is real and blocking when it occurs.

source_issues.title: [Feature]:agentscope封装的OpenAIChatModel.__call__方法中，漏掉了一些openai sdk会返回的参数
source_issues.evidence: Side-by-side comparison shows native OpenAI SDK returns finish_reason, tool_calls, function_call, and reasoning fields that agentscope wrapper omits. Users relying on these fields for downstream logic are affected.

signals.topic: Session I/O wrappers silently swallow DB exceptions and return None, causing permanent chat history loss
signals.summary: In _storage.py, read/write session wrapper functions catch all exceptions and return None instead of re-raising. When a transient DB failure occurs, callers cannot distinguish it from 'session not found', so they create a fresh empty AgentSession — permanently discarding all prior chat history. This is a silent data loss bug that provides no error signal to users.
aliases: DB exceptions swallowed in storage layer
signals.review_reason: This is a silent data loss bug: DB exceptions are caught and converted to None, making transient failures indistinguishable from 'session not found'. Users lose all chat history with no error signal. The bug is well-documented with specific code location (_storage.py wrappers), clear mechanism, and concrete impact on user data. Meets 'experience significantly degraded' and 'key data loss' criteria.

source_issues.title: Bug: session I/O wrappers in _storage.py swallow DB exceptions and return None, causing silent session data loss
source_issues.evidence: Wrapper functions catch all exceptions, log a warning, return None. When read_session returns None from a transient DB error, caller creates new empty AgentSession, silently discarding all prior chat history and session state.

signals.topic: Session deserialization crashes on empty runs and MCP ToolResult metadata is silently lost
signals.summary: AgentSession.from_dict and TeamSession.from_dict crash with an index error when the runs array is empty (direct runs[0] access without bounds check). Additionally, MCP CallToolResult.meta is not preserved during conversion to ToolResult, silently losing metadata for downstream consumers.
aliases: MCP metadata lost in ToolResult conversion
signals.review_reason: A P1 bug combining two distinct failures: a crash on an edge case (empty runs) causing main flow failure, and silent metadata loss from MCP responses. Both are reproducible and affect core session management. The crash is a clear 'main flow failure' and the metadata loss is 'data loss in a key function (MCP tool results)'.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Session deserialization crashes on empty runs and MCP ToolResult metadata is lost
source_issues.evidence: Two specific bugs: (1) from_dict crashes on runs=[] via direct array access without bounds check; (2) MCP CallToolResult.meta is not preserved when converting to ToolResult, causing metadata loss for downstream consumers.

signals.topic: Workflow cancellation is ineffective during acontinue_run due to missing araise_if_cancelled call in executor HITL path
signals.summary: When an Agent tool with external_execution runs inside a workflow step and acontinue_run is invoked, the workflow cannot be cancelled. The araise_if_cancelled function is never called in the executor HITL handling code path, so cancellation requests are ignored and the workflow continues to completion.
aliases: workflow cancellation blocked during HITL resume
signals.review_reason: Workflow cancellation being ineffective is a main flow blocking issue: users cannot stop a running workflow during the critical acontinue_run phase after HITL approval. The impact is significant (workflow runs to completion against user intent) and the fix location is precisely identified. This meets 'main flow failure' and 'key function blocked' criteria.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Workflow cancellation is ineffective during continue run
source_issues.evidence: araise_if_cancelled is not called in the code path handling executor HITL. When user requests cancellation during acontinue_run after tool approval, the workflow continues to completion regardless. The bug is isolated to executor HITL handling path.

signals.topic: AGUI interface drops multimodal image inputs before passing to Agent or Team, breaking vision use cases
signals.summary: The extract_agui_user_input function in agno/os/interfaces/agui/utils.py only extracts text parts from AG-UI multimodal UserMessage.content payloads, silently discarding image parts. Users who upload images through the AGUI interface see them lost before reaching the agent.
signals.review_reason: Multimodal image inputs being silently dropped from the AGUI interface is a 'key function unusable' issue for vision use cases. Users who upload images get zero error feedback and the images simply vanish. The bug is precisely located in extract_agui_user_input. This meets 'key function unavailable' criteria.

source_issues.title: [Bug] AGUI interface drops multimodal image inputs before calling Agent/Team
source_issues.evidence: extract_agui_user_input only handles text parts; image parts are silently dropped before agent/team invocation. Images are accepted by the AGUI protocol but never reach the model. Fix requires extracting images separately and passing via images= parameter.

signals.topic: Asynchronous continue run workflow mismatches sync cleanup_run, causing error with async Redis
signals.summary: When using an async Redis cancellation_manager, calling workflow.acontinue_run causes the error 'Sync Redis client not provided. Use async methods or provide a sync client.' The _acontinue_execute path uses synchronous cleanup_run instead of await acleanup_run, creating an async/sync mismatch.
aliases: acontinue_run calls sync cleanup with async Redis
signals.review_reason: An explicit error that breaks the async continue_run flow when async Redis is used. The mismatch causes a clear failure with a specific error message, representing a 'main flow failure' for async Redis users. Error is explicit and reproducible.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Asynchronous continue run workflow calls synchronous cleanup run and causes an error
source_issues.evidence: _acontinue_execute and _acontinue_execute_stream use synchronous cleanup_run instead of await acleanup_run, causing 'Sync Redis client not provided' error when async Redis is configured. This is an async/sync API mismatch in the continue run code path.

signals.topic: Title-agent hard-coded temperature 0.5 causes HTTP 400 API failures for models requiring specific temperature (Moonshot kimi-k2, GLM, MiniMax, Gemini, Qwen)
signals.summary: The built-in title agent hard-codes temperature 0.5, which short-circuits the model's required temperature transform. For models like Moonshot kimi-k2.* that strictly require temperature=1, the API returns HTTP 400, breaking session creation entirely.
signals.review_reason: User impact is clear: the title agent runs on every new session, and for affected model families it causes API 400 errors that block the session from being created. This is a main-flow failure with multiple model families impacted. Count=1 but evidence is specific and technical root cause is confirmed.

source_issues.title: Title-agent temperature 0.5 overrides model-required temperature, causing 400s on Moonshot kimi-k2.*
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model on Moonshot kimi-k2.*. Breaks any new session creation as the title agent runs automatically. Multiple model families affected (kimi-k2.*, glm-4.6/4.7, minimax-m2, gemini, qwen).

signals.topic: Chat window auto-scrolls while user is reading, making long conversations unreadable
signals.summary: During model output, the chat window auto-scrolls every ~30 seconds, forcibly jumping the reading position. Users can only read for ~10 seconds before being scrolled away, making it impossible to follow long conversations.
aliases: chat window jumps during model output
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation that makes reading long conversations impractical. Auto-scroll打断用户阅读体验，每次只能读10秒就被打断。桌面应用用户直接受影响。虽然count=1，但可复现步骤明确，影响持续存在。

source_issues.title: Chat Text automatically scrolls around
source_issues.evidence: User reports being able to read only 10 seconds before chat jumps to a different position. Affects Windows 11 Desktop App users. Reproducible by scrolling up during model output.

signals.topic: Accidental window close (Ctrl+W, Alt+F4, X button) on OpenCode Desktop kills all running tasks without confirmation
signals.summary: OpenCode Desktop closes immediately when Ctrl+W, Alt+F4, or the window X button is pressed, stopping all running tasks without any confirmation dialog. Users must manually restart all sessions and navigate back to all projects.
signals.review_reason: Work loss risk is real and the damage is high: all running tasks are killed, and the user must manually restart every session across all projects. The triggers (Ctrl+W, Alt+F4, X) are commonly used shortcuts, making accidental closure likely. This is a significant UX gap for a Desktop app.

source_issues.title: Are you sure you want to close Opencode? There are 7 active tasks running!
source_issues.evidence: User reports pressing Ctrl+W accidentally and losing all running tasks. Must reopen app, navigate to every project, and manually restart all conversations. Multiple methods of accidental close (Ctrl+W, Alt+F4, X button) all lack confirmation. Same user reported issue #27792 as well, indicating consistent usage.

signals.topic: Bash tool completely fails on Windows with PowerShell — 'paths[0]' property undefined error
signals.summary: On Windows with PowerShell, every bash tool invocation (ls, pwd, Get-ChildItem, dir) fails with 'The paths[0] property must be of type string, got undefined'. Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep tools work fine but bash tool is entirely non-functional.
aliases: bash tool broken on Windows PowerShell
signals.review_reason: Bash tool is a core tool used in virtually every coding session. On Windows PowerShell, it is completely broken — every command fails with the same internal validation error. This is a main-flow failure for Windows users. The fact that other AI coding agents work normally on the same machine confirms this is an opencode-specific bug. Priority P0 despite count=1 because bash tool failure blocks the primary coding workflow entirely.

source_issues.title: shell
source_issues.evidence: All bash tool commands (ls, pwd, Get-ChildItem, dir) fail with identical error on Windows 10/11 PowerShell. Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep tools work fine. Other AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor) work normally on the same machine, proving this is opencode-specific. Bash tool is a core tool used in nearly every coding session.

signals.topic: TUI high RAM consumption causes crashes/unusability on Linux
signals.summary: The OpenCode TUI consumes excessive RAM causing it to become unresponsive or crash. Reports from users on Arch Linux with foot terminal on version 1.14.48, with memory screenshots provided.
signals.review_reason: Excessive RAM consumption that makes the TUI unusable is a significant experience degradation and crash risk. While count=1, the issue is accompanied by a memory screenshot and was reported on a widely-used distribution (Arch Linux), suggesting it may affect others. Classified as P1 rather than P0 as it doesn't fully block usage but renders TUI unreliable.

source_issues.title: TUI consuming a lot of ram
source_issues.evidence: User reports high RAM consumption in v1.14.48 on Arch Linux with foot terminal. Memory screenshot provided showing elevated usage. Issue closed after 4 hours. Impact: TUI becomes unusable or crashes.

signals.topic: Files list API 不支持托管 Agent 文件列表查询（无法覆盖 beta header）
signals.summary: Managed Agent API 的文件列表功能因硬编码的默认 beta header（缺少 managed-agents-2026-04-01）而完全不可用，且无任何方式覆盖 header，导致用户无法在托管 Agent 场景下列举文件。
signals.review_reason: 该问题在 Managed Agent 文件列表场景下构成功能性阻断：用户无法在托管 Agent 场景下通过 SDK 列举文件，且无任何 workaround。属于关键功能不可用，符合用户痛点定义。虽然 count=1 不足以支撑 P0，但功能完全不可用且无变通方案，提升为 P1。

source_issues.title: Files list API does not support listing files from managed agent API
source_issues.evidence: Issue 明确描述 FileServiceImpl 对 managed agent 场景的 beta header 硬编码为默认值，缺少 managed-agents-2026-04-01，导致无法列出托管 Agent 关联的文件，且无任何 override 机制。

signals.topic: Prompt caching writes extra cache entries past explicit breakpoint, overbilling users at 1.25x rate for tokens never read
signals.summary: When using explicit cache_control breakpoint on system block, server writes additional cache entries in user content on warm calls. These writes are billed at 1.25x cache-write rate but are never read back, causing direct financial loss.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial loss via overbilling at 1.25x rate. Every warm call with an explicit breakpoint incurs unrequested cache writes. Issue reproduces across SDK versions and affects all users relying on explicit cache_control — not edge-case specific. Clear cost impact with empirical evidence.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Server writes additional cache entries past explicit `cache_control` breakpoint, billing 1.25x for tokens that are never read
source_issues.evidence: Warm calls write ~1416 extra tokens to cache at 1.25x rate with zero cache_read on those tokens. Per-call financial overcharge confirmed with repro script showing cache_creation=1416 on warm calls where only 1 breakpoint exists.

signals.topic: tool_runner loop infinite hangs when append_messages() called inside iteration
signals.summary: The 'Advanced usage' example in official docs causes infinite loop. Calling runner.append_messages(user_message) inside the tool-runner loop sets _messages_modified=True, preventing auto-append of tool results, causing Claude to re-invoke the same tool indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: users following official 'Advanced usage' documentation experience infinite loop with no resolution. App hangs until manually killed. Affects all users who follow the documented pattern — not an obscure edge case.

source_issues.title: [Bug] append_messages() inside tool runner loop causes infinite loop (advanced usage docs example)
source_issues.evidence: Infinite loop reproduced using official 'Advanced usage' docs example. Tool result never reaches history, causing app to hang indefinitely. The 'Modifying tool results' example on same page correctly uses append_messages(message, tool_response), confirming the pattern inconsistency.

signals.topic: ServerToolResult content blocks orphaned when client tools interrupt streaming, causing stuck UI spinners
signals.summary: When Messages API returns stop_reason=tool_use (requesting client tool execution) while server-side tools code_execution/web_search are running concurrently, the ServerToolResult blocks for server tools are never delivered, causing orphaned tool_use blocks.
signals.review_reason: Key functionality broken for concurrent server+client tool usage: ServerToolResult never delivered, UI stuck in 'running' state. Production load test evidence confirms widespread impact across concurrent workloads.

source_issues.title: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt the stream (code_execution + client tool concurrency)
source_issues.evidence: Production load test evidence: text_editor_code_execution and web_search results never delivered in streaming events or get_final_message(). Frontend spinners stuck forever. Monitoring/load tests flag as failures even though operation succeeded. Workaround requires synthetic tool_result events.

signals.topic: Managed Agents sessions.events.send rejects output_config (effort parameter), causing 3x cost and 3.3x latency vs Messages API parity
signals.summary: The managed-agents sessions.events.send endpoint returns HTTP 400 when output_config.effort is passed, while messages.create accepts it. Users cannot control thinking depth on managed agents, forced to use opaque platform defaults.
aliases: thinking effort control unavailable managed agents
signals.review_reason: Significant cost loss (3x) and latency increase (3.3x) due to missing API parity. User cannot use effort parameter on managed agents despite GA availability on messages.create. Affects all managed-agents users on Sonnet 4.6+.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents `sessions.events.send` rejects `output_config` with 400 — no parity with `messages.create` for effort/thinking control
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 from server-side strict validation. Smoke trace shows 3x cost ($0.31 vs $0.10) and 3.3x latency (156s vs 47s active time) on Sonnet 4.6 procedural workloads when effort cannot be tuned.

signals.topic: files.beta.upload mutates caller's dict in place via deepcopy_minimal, causing silent caller-side data corruption
signals.summary: deepcopy_minimal does not recursively copy tuples, only lists and dicts. When files.beta.upload receives a FileTypes tuple with a Mapping as its 4th element, that mapping is mutated in place and returned to the caller changed.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption: caller's dict mutated without warning, potentially causing cascading bugs in downstream code. While fixable on caller side, this violates the principle of least surprise for an SDK API.

source_issues.title: Use of `deepcopy_minimal` in `files.beta.upload` mutates dict in place
source_issues.evidence: Empirically verified: headers dict within FileTypes tuple is mutated in place after calling files.beta.upload. Caller's original data structure corrupted silently.

signals.topic: Vertex SDK: URL source document blocks rejected with misleading error path
signals.summary: When using @anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk to send document content blocks with URL sources, the request is rejected. The returned error references the wrong field (image.source.base64.data), making debugging extremely difficult. URL sources are documented as supported but are rejected by the Vertex endpoint.
aliases: document URL sources not supported on Vertex
wrong error path for URL source documents
signals.review_reason: This is a user-blocking issue: the Vertex SDK rejects a documented feature (URL source document blocks) with a misleading error path that points to the wrong field, making the root cause hard to identify. While count=1 prevents P0, the dual problem (feature rejection + error path confusion) represents a significant workflow disruption for Vertex SDK users.

source_issues.title: Vertex AI: document URL sources rejected with incorrect error path
source_issues.evidence: User attempts to send a document content block with URL source via Vertex SDK; request is rejected with error 'messages.0.content.0.image.source.base64.data: URL sources are not supported'. Error field path points to wrong location (image.source.base64.data) for a document block with source type url, severely hindering debugging.

signals.topic: zodOutputFormat helper throws when used with zod v3 schemas
signals.summary: The zodOutputFormat helper function throws an exception when passed a zod v3 schema, making the feature completely unusable for any project that has upgraded to zod v3.
signals.review_reason: zodOutputFormat is a shipped helper that throws on zod v3 schemas, causing complete feature unavailability for users on the v3 major version. The failure is explicit (try/catch needed to avoid crashes) and affects a core SDK helper. Count=1 prevents P0, but the impact is unambiguous feature breakage.

source_issues.title: zodOutputFormat fails when project uses zod3
source_issues.evidence: Calling zodOutputFormat(Schema3) with a zod v3 schema throws an exception, while zod v4 schemas work fine. This breaks the zodOutputFormat feature for all users on zod v3, a major version with significant adoption.

signals.topic: StructuredOutput tool intermittently wraps response in extra 'output' field causing schema validation to fail
signals.summary: When using output_format with StructuredOutput, the tool non-deterministically wraps user data in an {"output": {...}} field. This causes schema validation to fail, ResultMessage.structured_output to be None, and Claude to receive conflicting signals (both 'required property missing' and 'additional property forbidden' at once), leading it to degrade output (e.g., 47 items reduced to 1).
signals.review_reason: Non-deterministic StructuredOutput wrapping is a main-flow blocker. Schema validation fails intermittently, ResultMessage.structured_output becomes None unpredictably, and Claude's internal state is corrupted by conflicting schema errors, causing it to silently degrade output quality. This is a primary feature (structured output) failure with direct user-visible impact.

source_issues.title: [BUG] StructuredOutput tool wraps data in 'output' field causing schema validation to fail
source_issues.evidence: Non-deterministic wrapping in {"output": {...}}. ResultMessage.structured_output is None when wrapper present. Agent sees conflicting schema errors: 'required property actions missing' AND 'additional property output forbidden'. Claude responds by reducing output from 47 items to 1 item.

signals.topic: Error context destroyed through exception flattening — CLI failures produce only unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1' without actionable details
signals.summary: When the Claude CLI subprocess exits with a non-zero code, the SDK destroys all error context through a 3-step chain: ProcessError is created with hardcoded 'Check stderr output for details' instead of actual stderr, then flattened via str() stripping all exception attributes, then re-raised as bare Exception() destroying the original type. Consumer code that catches ClaudeSDKError never fires, and users cannot diagnose why their CLI process failed.
signals.review_reason: CLI subprocess failures are a primary use case for the SDK (embedding Claude Code CLI). When they fail, the only error message users see is the uninformative 'Command failed with exit code 1 (exit code: 1)' with no stderr content, no typed exception, and no way to diagnose root cause. This blocks debugging entirely and is the #1 support friction point.

source_issues.title: Error context destroyed through exception flattening — CLI failures produce unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1'
source_issues.evidence: 3-step chain: subprocess_cli.py hardcodes stderr='Check stderr output for details', query.py flattens via str() stripping exit_code/stderr attrs, query.py re-raises bare Exception() instead of ClaudeSDKError. Consumer 'except ClaudeSDKError' blocks never fire. No actionable diagnostic available for CLI failures.

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage fires prematurely while subagent is still executing tool calls, causing cascading downstream failures
signals.summary: When an orchestrator dispatches multiple subagents in parallel via the Task tool, the SDK occasionally delivers TaskNotificationMessage (as <task-notification> SystemMessage) while the referenced subagent is still mid-execution. The orchestrator interprets the notification as a completion signal and dispatches downstream reviewers against output files that don't exist yet. This causes entire agent pipelines to run on stale or missing data, wasting compute and credits.
aliases: subagent completion signal fires too early
orchestrator misreceives TASK_DONE before subagent finishes
signals.review_reason: Premature task notifications are a main-flow blocker for the primary orchestration use case (parallel subagent dispatch). The orchestrator's event-driven pattern depends on reliable completion signals; when the signal fires early, downstream work is dispatched against empty state, causing wasted compute, wasted credits ($21+ per incident), and requiring manual intervention. Clear cascading failure with financial impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Non-deterministic reproduction: 5 subagents dispatched in parallel, premature notifications fired 76-850 seconds before actual completion. Result: 5 downstream reviewer agents dispatched against non-existent output files. Original researchers re-dispatched (8 min wasted). Actual TASK_DONE arrived 17 min later. Total: 32 min / $21.51 vs baseline 51 min / $22.33. Direct cost loss and compute waste.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely when CLI subprocess shutdown handler blocks, blocking 30% of parallel SDK jobs
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport.close() sends SIGTERM to the Claude Code subprocess and then calls process.wait() with no timeout. When the Node.js process runs a shutdown handler that blocks (e.g., waiting for an MCP server or subagent to exit), process.wait() blocks forever. This causes the entire Python worker process to hang indefinitely, leading to VM infrastructure timeouts.
signals.review_reason: close() indefinite hang is a process-blocking defect that affects 30% of jobs in the primary deployment pattern (parallel SDK instances). The SDK job completes successfully but the worker process never exits, causing VM infrastructure timeouts. This is a direct operational blocker with quantifiable failure rate in production-scale use.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely if subprocess shutdown handler blocks
source_issues.evidence: Running ~200 parallel Claude Code instances via SDK. 30% of jobs hung indefinitely — Claude Code job finished successfully but VM stayed hanging because transport.close() never returned. Entire worker process hit VM infra timeout. Impact explicitly quantified at 30% job failure rate.

signals.topic: stderr callback exception silently kills the entire _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines for the rest of the session
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport._handle_stderr wraps an async for loop in a single 'except Exception: pass' outside the loop. When the user-provided options.stderr callback raises even once, the exception is caught at the outer level, the loop terminates, and no further stderr lines are delivered for the rest of the session. The error is completely silent with no log, no traceback, and no indication that anything went wrong.
aliases: stderr loop terminates on callback error
stderr piping permanently disabled after single error
silent stderr drop after callback exception
signals.review_reason: stderr callback error permanently disables stderr piping for the entire session, silently. This means all subsequent CLI errors (permission denied, crashes, warnings) are invisible to the user. This is a significant debugging trap — users relying on stderr for observability get no feedback when the callback first raises, and all future errors are silently swallowed. Non-obvious failure mode that directly impairs production debugging.

source_issues.title: Bug: stderr callback raise silently kills _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer: mock stderr stream with 2 lines, callback raises RuntimeError on first line. count = 1 (second line dropped). 5/5 reproduction. Subsequent CLI errors that would reach the user's logger are permanently lost. Silent failure — no log, no traceback, no indication that anything went wrong.

signals.topic: Linux glibc 系统上 SDK 二进制解析器错误选择 musl 变体导致 spawn ENOENT
signals.summary: 在 glibc Linux 系统（如 GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest）上，SDK 的原生二进制解析器优先尝试 musl 变体包，当 pnpm 同时安装 musl 和 glibc 两个可选依赖时（pnpm 10 的 libc 过滤不完善），require.resolve 成功解析 musl 路径，但 spawn 时因动态链接器缺失（/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1）而失败，ENOENT 错误导致主流程 query() 完全阻断。
aliases: glibc 系统 musl 二进制优先
signals.review_reason: 3 条独立 issue 均确认在 glibc Linux 上主流程 query() 因二进制选择错误完全阻断，影响 CI/CD 场景（GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest），用户必须手动传递 pathToClaudeCodeExecutable 绕过，为高频阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: spawn ENOENT 导致 query() 完全失败；复现于 Ubuntu 24.04 glibc 2.39；需要手动传 pathToClaudeCodeExecutable 绕过

source_issues.title: Binary picker selects musl variant on glibc Linux, causing ENOENT at spawn
source_issues.evidence: 复现于 v0.2.138 Ubuntu 24.04 glibc 2.39；musl 包缺少 libc 字段导致 npm 10 也安装了错误变体

source_issues.title: Native binary resolver picks linux-x64-musl on glibc systems, ignoring the libc field
source_issues.evidence: 复现于 v0.2.126 和 v0.2.138；pnpm 10 下 30-50% 缓存未命中时触发；spawn ENOENT 后 glibc 回退逻辑未到达

signals.topic: createSdkMcpServer 使用 Zod v4 时丢失嵌套属性和动态注册工具的 .describe() 元数据
signals.summary: 当使用 Zod v4 时，createSdkMcpServer 的工具输入 schema 中，嵌套属性的 .describe() 和通过 registerTool 动态注册的工具的 .describe() 均被丢弃，导致 MCP tools/list 返回的 schema 缺少 description 字段，AI 模型无法获得字段级指导信息，降低工具可用性。
aliases: Zod v4 schema metadata lost in MCP tools
signals.review_reason: 2 条 issue 覆盖了 Zod v4 兼容性缺口的不同场景（顶层 vs 嵌套 vs 动态注册），均已提供最小复现和根因分析。虽 count=2 未达 P0，但关键工具 schema 描述丢失直接影响 AI 模型对工具参数的理解，属于显著功能退化。

source_issues.title: createSdkMcpServer drops Zod v4 field .describe() metadata from tool inputSchema
source_issues.evidence: Zod v4 场景下工具属性描述全部丢失；降级 Zod v3 可恢复；已知 Zod v4 peerDependency 兼容性缺口

source_issues.title: createSdkMcpServer drops Zod v4 field .describe() if nested or added after via registerTool
source_issues.evidence: 嵌套属性和 registerTool 动态注册工具的描述均被丢弃；根因为 createSdkMcpServer 仅在创建时做单层遍历

signals.topic: close() 在首次 assistant 消息之前调用导致 session 变为不可恢复状态
signals.summary: 在新会话中，如果在收到首次 assistant 消息之前调用 close() 回调，返回的 session_id 将不可恢复，再次使用该 session_id 调用 query(resume: ...) 会收到 'No conversation found' 错误，直接破坏了会话恢复这一核心特性的可用性，与 AbortController 行为不一致。
aliases: session not resumable after early close()
session_id not persisted on early close
signals.review_reason: 核心功能（session resume）违反行为一致性原则，在特定时序下会话不可恢复。用户需要额外检测逻辑来规避，无开箱即用解决方案。虽 count=1，但属于主流程功能破坏性 bug，有明确复现路径。

source_issues.title: Bug: Calling `close()` before first assistant message makes session non-resumable
source_issues.evidence: 直接违反会话恢复契约；AbortController 在相同场景下可正常恢复；用户需自行检测 assistant 消息是否已收到来绕过；提供 gist 复现脚本

signals.topic: options.hooks 导致 agent 忽略自定义 systemPrompt，错误标识为 'Claude Code'
signals.summary: 当传入任意类型的 hooks（PreToolUse、PostToolUse、SessionEnd、PreCompact）时，agent 在回答身份类问题时忽略自定义 systemPrompt 中的 persona 定义，错误地响应为 'Claude Code' 或通用 AI 助手。即使用空 handler 也会触发，覆盖所有 hook 类型。生产多智能体系统面临在身份保真度和可观测性之间二选一的困境。
signals.review_reason: 生产多智能体系统中核心需求（自定义 persona + 可观测性 hooks）不可兼得，身份错误在企业场景中具有品牌和合规影响。虽 count=1，但用户明确指出影响 17-agent 生产系统，发现过程耗时 8 小时，属于严重体验降级。有确定复现和部分 workaround（canUseTool）但覆盖不完整。

source_issues.title: options.hooks causes agent to ignore custom systemPrompt and identify as "Claude Code"
source_issues.evidence: 在 17-agent 企业系统中发现；任何 hook 类型（包括空 handler）均触发；确定性复现；可观测性与身份保真度被迫二选一；canUseTool 回调可作为部分替代但不支持 PostToolUse/PreCompact/SessionEnd

signals.topic: restoreConfigFromBase crashes with ENOENT on symlinked or CLAUDE.md-only PRs, breaking all reviews
signals.summary: cpSync in restoreConfigFromBase fails with ENOENT when sensitive paths are git-tracked symlinks, or when only CLAUDE.md exists without .claude/ directory. Action exits code 1 on every affected PR — no review can run. Regression from v1.0.89.
aliases: cpSync symlink ENOENT on sensitive files
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: action crashes (exit code 1) on any PR where CLAUDE.md is a symlink or where .claude/ is absent. Three independent reports (#1187, #1220, #1311) confirm a regression introduced in v1.0.89 that makes code review entirely unavailable for affected repos. Workaround of pinning to v1.0.88 is known but means missing all subsequent fixes.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase crashes with ENOENT when only CLAUDE.md exists (cpSync needs mkdir of .claude-pr/ first)
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with ENOENT on PRs with CLAUDE.md but no .claude directory; cpSync fails to create parent directory .claude-pr/ before copying single file; action exits with code 1; workaround is pinning back to v1.0.88; affects all users with CLAUDE.md-only setups; confirmed regression from v1.0.89.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes during restoreConfigFromBase with ENOENT symlink when sensitive paths like CLAUDE.md are symlinks; 100% reproducible on every review run; action exits with code 1; workaround is pinning to v1.0.88.

source_issues.title: cpSync fails on symlinked sensitive files
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with ENOENT symlink error when CLAUDE.md is a git-tracked symlink to AGENTS.md; every Code Review run fails 100% reproducibly; no workaround exists; cross-references #1187 as same root cause.

signals.topic: GitHub Copilot SWE agent actor causes action to crash with 404 at multiple permission-check code paths
signals.summary: GITHUB_ACTOR=Copilot (no [bot] suffix) causes 404 errors at both checkWritePermissions and checkHumanActor, making allowed_bots bypass unreachable. Three separate failure modes across two code paths.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking across three distinct reports: action crashes with 404 at multiple code paths when GitHub Copilot SWE agent triggers a workflow. The allowed_bots bypass is unreachable because crashes happen first. No practical workaround — users building Copilot-Claude review triage pipelines are entirely blocked.

source_issues.title: Action fails with 'Not Found' when triggered by GitHub Copilot (actor Copilot returns 404 from /users/ API)
source_issues.evidence: checkHumanActor crashes with 404 when GITHUB_ACTOR=Copilot (SWE agent); GET /users/Copilot returns 404 because Copilot is not a resolvable GitHub user; crash occurs before allowed_bots logic is consulted so allowed_bots:'*' has no effect; action exits code 1.

source_issues.title: checkWritePermissions fails with 404 for non-user actors like Copilot
source_issues.evidence: checkWritePermissions calls octokit.repos.getCollaboratorPermissionLevel() with Copilot as username; API returns 404 because Copilot is not a GitHub user; action fails before any review can run; bot bypass only checks for [bot] suffix but Copilot does not follow that convention.

source_issues.title: allowed_bots bypasses actor check but not permission check — bot actors still fail with 404
source_issues.evidence: allowed_bots correctly bypasses checkHumanActor for Copilot but checkWritePermissions still calls the collaborators API which returns 404 for non-user actors; action fails with 'Actor does not have write permissions'.

signals.topic: Workflow validation fails silently when base branch name contains # character
signals.summary: Action's workflow validation truncates the branch name at #, causing a file-not-found lookup and skipping the review without error indication.
aliases: hash in branch name workflow skip
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking with no error indication: the action silently skips review on branches with valid # in the name, showing only a warning. Users cannot tell from the action output that the branch name is the cause.

source_issues.title: workflow validation failed if base branch's name has # in it
source_issues.evidence: When default branch name contains # (e.g. feat/#689-v1.2.0), action fails with workflow validation error; action skips with a warning and exits without running review; main flow blocked; GitHub itself accepts # in branch names.

signals.topic: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with end_turn and empty result, silently producing no work while reporting success
signals.summary: Model makes file changes then voluntarily halts with stop_reason:end_turn and empty result. Zero Bash invocations, pending TodoWrite items, no PR created — yet action returns outcome:success. Dangerous silent failure for orchestrating workflows.
signals.review_reason: Dangerous silent failure: the action returns outcome:success with no error indication, but zero Bash invocations occur and no work product is produced across 7 reproducible runs. Orchestrating workflows cannot distinguish success from failure without inspecting logs.

source_issues.title: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason: end_turn, never invokes Bash; multi-step prompts fail to complete (claude-sonnet-4-6)
source_issues.evidence: Agent makes Edit/Write calls then halts with stop_reason:end_turn and empty result string, never invoking Bash; action returns outcome:success despite 0 Bash invocations; reproducible across 7 runs in ~14 hours with byte-identical prompts; naive workflows treat green check as successful completion.

signals.topic: Ephemeral .claude-pr/ snapshot directory is accidentally committed to PR branch on bot fix-up commits
signals.summary: restoreConfigFromBase creates .claude-pr/ as a runner-side artifact but git add -A in the CLI's commit stage picks it up, creating stealth chore commits not acknowledged in the bot reply.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation with hidden user impact: ephemeral .claude-pr/ runner-side snapshot is unintentionally committed to the user's repository, creating stealth commits that pollute the PR history. The bot's reply provides no signal that extra commits were made.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase snapshot at .claude-pr/ gets committed to PR branch when bot pushes a fix
source_issues.evidence: On @claude fix-up requests in PR context, .claude-pr/ snapshot directory is accidentally committed to the PR branch via git add -A; bot reply only mentions the requested fix with no mention of the .claude-pr/ commit; results in stealth chore commits unrelated to the PR; requires manual git rm --cached cleanup.

signals.topic: Garbled/corrupted text output in CLI terminal display — regression affecting all output throughout sessions
signals.summary: Terminal display shows severe text corruption (random symbols, garbled characters, corrupted ASCII table borders) affecting all prompts, user input, Claude output, and status messages. Affects entire session with no readable sections.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users on the same day report complete terminal display corruption — all prompts, input, and Claude output rendered as gibberish. This is a high-severity UX regression (the entire tool becomes nearly unusable for reading output). Both reports are on the latest version (2.1.142, released 2026-05-14), indicating a recent regression that shipped to all users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] CC Terminal display corrupted with garbled characters throughout every single session
source_issues.evidence: Both prompts and Claude output render as gibberish. ASCII table borders corrupted. Corruption is persistent across entire session with no readable sections. Two separate reports on the same day.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Garbled text output in CLI display
source_issues.evidence: Garbled text reported as of past few days, affecting all output. Confirmed on v2.1.142 (most recent release). Error log shows EISDIR on directory read in entrypoints/cli.js.

signals.topic: PTY master file descriptor leak on macOS causing system-wide terminal exhaustion
signals.summary: Claude Code leaks /dev/ptmx master FDs across tool invocations; long sessions exhaust macOS kern.tty.ptmx_max (default 511), causing forkpty() to fail system-wide — Terminal.app, sudo, SSH, and Claude's own Bash/Agent all break until machine reboot.
signals.review_reason: This is a resource exhaustion bug with severe system-wide impact: after ~511 Claude tool invocations, forkpty() fails for the ENTIRE machine, blocking sudo, SSH, Terminal.app, and Claude's own agent/Bash tool. The 'has repro' label and detailed kernel-level evidence (lsof output, ENXIO errno) confirm a real, reproducible bug. While the primary in-file report is labeled duplicate, it references the root cause bug; the impact is unambiguous — the entire terminal subsystem becomes unusable.

source_issues.title: PTY master FDs leak on long sessions — exhausts kern.tty.ptmx_max on macOS
source_issues.evidence: FD count grows monotonically on every tool call; lsof confirms /dev/ptmx FDs never released after child exits. System-wide ENXIO after ~511 sessions blocks ALL terminal usage including critical system tools (sudo, ssh).

signals.topic: MCP tools pagination — tools on page 2+ of tools/list silently dropped after initial fetch and after ToolListChangedNotification
signals.summary: When MCP servers return paginated tools/list responses with nextCursor, Claude Code only fetches the first page. All tools on subsequent pages return 'No such tool available' with no warning. This silently breaks MCP integrations with >20 tools.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional core breakdown: MCP is a primary extensibility mechanism, and tool pagination is part of the MCP spec. When tools are dropped silently (no error on fetch, just 'No such tool available' at call time), users cannot reason about whether a tool doesn't exist or was dropped. This breaks MCP integration completeness for any server with >20 tools, which is a common real-world scenario. The silent failure mode makes this especially painful — users may not realize why certain commands fail.

source_issues.title: MCP tools on page 2+ of paginated tools/list dropped after ToolListChangedNotification
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproduction: MCP server with 29 tools (6 on page 1, 23 on page 2 via nextCursor) — page 2 tools are silently never fetched. User-facing error is 'No such tool available' with no indication that the tool exists on the server but was dropped by CC's pagination handling.

signals.topic: Cowork: user messages stuck in pulsating in-flight animation after session switching — regression on macOS
signals.summary: After sending a follow-up message in session A while Claude is mid-response and switching back, the user message remains in the pulsating in-flight state permanently for the session lifetime. Claude's response is complete and session is responsive — only the UI state is stuck.
signals.review_reason: This is a UI state bug affecting the Cowork feature (collaborative use case). The stuck animation is persistent for the session lifetime and clearly user-visible. It is explicitly identified as a regression of a prior fix, linking to 3 earlier issues in the same cluster — indicating this is a recurring, unsolved problem. Non-blocking but degrading UX.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork: User messages remain in pulsating in-flight state after session-switch — regression / incomplete-fix variant of the #26805 / #26921 / #44776 cluster (macOS, May 2026)
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly links to 3 prior issues in the same bug cluster (#26805, #26921, #44776). The issue is a known regression pattern, indicating a persistent unsolved problem across multiple releases. The pulsating animation persists for the entire session lifetime once triggered.

signals.topic: Azure AD authentication blocked — server-side app registration misconfiguration (AADSTS900971)
signals.summary: Enterprise users with Azure AD SSO cannot authenticate due to misconfigured redirect URIs in Anthropic's Azure AD app registration. The error AADSTS900971 (no redirect URI configured) blocks entire enterprise login flows.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete auth flow blocker for enterprise Azure AD users. The root cause is in Anthropic's own Azure AD app registration (server-side, not user-configurable), so affected users cannot self-resolve. While labeled 'needs-info', the user's analysis of the error code (AADSTS900971) and client ID definitively identifies the problem as Anthropic-side misconfiguration.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Server-side configuration issue with Anthropic's Azure AD app registration, not a port problem.
source_issues.evidence: User correctly identifies this as a server-side configuration issue in Anthropic's own Azure AD app registration (client ID 08ad6f98-a4f8-4635-bb8d-f1a3044760f0). The redirect URI is not registered, blocking authentication for all Azure AD enterprise users with that configuration.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook broken due to deprecated assistant message prefill API
signals.summary: The summarization notebook (capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb) crashes with BadRequestError when users run cell 8, because the notebook uses assistant message prefill which is now deprecated. The error message is: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' This blocks the main learning flow of the cookbook.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because the official Anthropic summarization cookbook — a primary learning resource — is completely broken and cannot be run end-to-end. Users hitting cell 8 encounter a BadRequestError that blocks the main learning flow. The prefill pattern was silently deprecated, and the cookbook was not updated, leaving users with a non-functional learning artifact. While count=1 (single repo), the impact is a main workflow blocker for cookbook users, justifying P2.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: Full BadRequestError traceback when running notebook cell 8. Error: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' Users cannot complete the summarization cookbook guide.

signals.topic: skill-creator scripts completely unusable on Windows due to multiple POSIX-only bugs
signals.summary: Three issues in the skill-creator plugin describe a systemic Windows compatibility failure that makes the core description-optimization workflow fail completely, burning 300-900K tokens per iteration for zero usable output.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues in the same plugin all blocking core workflows on Windows. Issue 1875 and 1850 describe complete tool failure (0 usable output, wasted tokens). Issue 1863 blocks the packaging step. Combined, these represent a systemic Windows compatibility failure that makes the skill-creator plugin unusable for the large Windows developer user base.

source_issues.title: skill-creator description optimizer (run_loop.py) unusable on Windows — 4+ POSIX-only assumptions
source_issues.evidence: 4 independent POSIX-only bugs: subprocess can't find claude.CMD, select.select fails on pipes, read_text/write_text uses cp1252 encoding, stdin pipes encode with cp1252. All 60 queries fail, 0 triggers, run aborts.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop.py / run_eval.py description optimizer is non-functional on Windows (5 distinct bugs + recall=0% even after compat patches)
source_issues.evidence: 5 distinct Windows bugs: cp1252 read_text crash, UTF-8 BOM breaks frontmatter, subprocess can't find claude.CMD, select.select broken on pipes, subprocess stalls on permission prompts. Even after patching all 5, recall=0%. Burns 300-900K tokens per iteration for no signal.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: package_skill.py crashes on Windows (emoji print + cp1252 stdout)
source_issues.evidence: Crashes immediately on Windows with UnicodeEncodeError when printing emoji (U+1F4E6 PACKAGE). Workaround requires -X utf8 flag not documented in SKILL.md workflow.

signals.topic: Published plugins not appearing on claude.com/plugins marketplace despite 'Published' status
signals.summary: Plugins show 'Published' status on the submissions page but are invisible on claude.com/plugins. No confirmation email is received. Users invest time creating and submitting plugins that remain undiscoverable.
signals.review_reason: Key feature unavailable — plugins marked as 'Published' are not discoverable in the public marketplace. This defeats the entire purpose of the publishing workflow. Users invest time creating and submitting plugins only to find them invisible to the intended audience. Two independent reports indicate this is a systemic issue, not an isolated case.

source_issues.title: Plugin marked as 'Published' on submissions but not visible on claude.com/plugins
source_issues.evidence: Plugin sentry-error-assistant shows 'Published' status on submissions page but returns 'Nothing to see here' on claude.com/plugins. Not listed in plugin directory. No confirmation email received. Related issue #1272 reports same problem.

source_issues.title: Published plugin 'Magician' not visible for weeks following post-publish
source_issues.evidence: Plugin 'Magician' has been in 'Published' state since April 17th but is still not visible on claude.com/plugins. Plugin page at github.com/Alexander-Tyagunov/magician exists but the plugin is not accessible from the official marketplace.

signals.topic: Hookify rules silently fail to load or block without giving the agent the reason
signals.summary: Two independent silent-failure modes: PreToolUse/PostToolUse blocks don't set permissionDecisionReason for the agent, causing wasteful retry loops; and relative glob in config_loader.py makes rules silently dead when CWD ≠ project root, with 4 pre-existing rules dead for weeks.
signals.review_reason: Hookify enforcement silently fails in two independent ways: (1) blocks don't tell the agent WHY they were blocked, causing wasteful retry loops; (2) relative glob makes rules silently dead when CWD ≠ project root. Both are worst-case failure modes for an enforcement tool — users believe their rules are active when they are not. Issue 1859 explicitly notes 4 pre-existing rules were dead for weeks before discovery.

source_issues.title: hookify: PreToolUse/PostToolUse block path leaves permissionDecisionReason unset — agent never receives the rule body
source_issues.evidence: When hookify blocks a tool via PreToolUse/PostToolUse, it sets systemMessage (user sees why) but leaves permissionDecisionReason unset for the agent. Agent receives only generic 'Hook PreToolUse:Edit denied this tool' and retries wastefully without knowing the rule body or what alternative to use.

source_issues.title: hookify: relative glob in config_loader.py makes rules silently dead when plugin hook CWD ≠ project root
source_issues.evidence: config_loader.py uses relative glob '.claude/hookify.*.local.md' which depends on CWD. When Claude Code invokes plugin hooks from a CWD ≠ project root, the glob matches nothing and returns empty rules silently. No error, no warning, rules just don't fire. User assumes enforcement is active when it isn't. 4 pre-existing rules were silently dead for weeks in reporter's project.

signals.topic: Plugins hardcode ~/.claude/ path ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / XDG compliance causing silent failures
signals.summary: session-report and security-guidance plugins hardcode ~/.claude/ paths. When CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR redirects to ~/.config/claude/, session-report finds no sessions (silent empty results) and security-guidance creates stale directories in wrong location.
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation for users who use XDG-compliant config directories. The session-report tool fails to find sessions when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set (tool silently returns empty results). security-guidance creates stale directories in the wrong location. Both violate the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR contract, and the silent failure in session-report means users get no signal that data is being looked for in the wrong place.

source_issues.title: session-report: hardcodes ~/.claude/projects — must support CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
source_issues.evidence: session-report plugin hardcodes '~/.claude/projects' path. When CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR redirects to ~/.config/claude/, the tool looks in the wrong directory and finds no sessions.

source_issues.title: security-guidance: hardcodes ~/.claude/ — must respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
source_issues.evidence: security-guidance hook hardcodes ~/.claude/ for state files (lines 131, 137). When CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set, creates stale ~/.claude/ directories instead of using the configured location.

signals.topic: Discord channel plugin exits before gateway login completes due to stdin EOF race condition
signals.summary: Plugin process exits via process.exit(0) when Claude Code's MCP stdio bridge closes stdin within milliseconds of the initialize handshake, before Discord gateway login finishes. Bot stays offline, inbound messages never inject.
signals.review_reason: Core Discord channel functionality fails silently — bot never connects to Discord gateway, so inbound channel messages cannot inject into the Claude Code session. This is a main flow failure where the plugin process exits before any useful work can happen. The intermittent nature makes it especially painful to debug.

source_issues.title: discord channel plugin: stdin EOF triggers shutdown before gateway login completes
source_issues.evidence: Plugin exits via process.exit(0) when Claude Code's MCP stdio bridge closes stdin's write side, which happens within milliseconds of the initialize handshake — before client.login() finishes the Discord WebSocket handshake. Bot stays offline, inbound messages never inject. Intermittent but reproducible.

signals.topic: README 中的示例快速入门链接失效（404），导致用户无法访问 Browser Tools API Demo 页面
signals.summary: README.md 中指向 browser-tools-api-demo 的链接返回 404，用户点击后无法访问目标页面，主流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: README 中链接失效导致用户无法访问目标快速入门示例，属于主流程阻断（404 直接中断学习路径），有截图和用户评论证据，属于真实用户痛点。因 count=1 且非多仓问题，优先级定为 P2。

source_issues.title: Documentation: Broken link in README
source_issues.evidence: README.md 中指向 browser-tools-api-demo 的链接点击后返回 404 page not found，用户无法访问该快速入门资源，且有截图证据。

signals.topic: ToolUse API lacks scalability for large-scale chunked output processing
signals.summary: Users building multi-pass workflows to process large datasets encounter context window exhaustion and ambiguous tool_result/tool_use sequencing requirements, causing workflow failures and API errors.
signals.review_reason: Issue #14 describes a real workflow-blocking problem: the user cannot scale a multi-pass summarization pipeline because the API requires resending full context on each tool_result call, leading to context window exhaustion and an invalid_request_error. This causes the user's main use case (cumulative document summarization) to fail. Single-occurrence, single-repo, but user impact is clearly documented — confirmed workflow failure + API error. Marked P2 because count=1 does not meet P0/P1 threshold for frequency.

source_issues.title: ToolUse : How to use tools to scalably chunk output beyond output token limit?
source_issues.evidence: User reports receiving 'invalid_request_error: messages.0: tool_result block(s) provided when previous message does not contain any tool_use blocks' error. User describes being forced to resend entire conversation history (already at 150k/200k tokens) on each tool_result call, causing context window exhaustion. User explicitly states scalability is 'in jeopardy'.

signals.topic: No native mechanism to share Claude skills across a team — per-machine storage causes sync friction
signals.summary: Claude skills are stored per-machine at `~/.claude/skills/`, with no built-in team sharing or registry mechanism. Teams using Claude across multiple machines must manually re-sync skills for each new engineer, creating maintenance drift and onboarding friction for teams of 5+ engineers.
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (one from January, one current) independently describe the same friction: per-machine skill storage forces manual, non-native synchronization for any team larger than one person. This is not an edge case — it is a structural limitation that every multi-engineer team encounters. While it does not block individual use, it creates ongoing operational overhead and onboarding delays. The sustained activity on issue #228 (13 comments over months) confirms this is a persistent, widespread pain point rather than a one-off complaint.

source_issues.title: docs: any guidance on sharing SKILL.md across a team?
source_issues.evidence: User reports hitting the friction point 'pretty fast' at ~5 engineers. Per-machine ~/.claude/skills/ means adding a new skill requires everyone to re-sync manually. User tried git submodules (breaks for teammates), dotfiles sync (drifts after weeks), and a self-hosted 60s-loop registry — all workarounds, none native.

source_issues.title: Enable org-wide skill sharing in Claude.ai
source_issues.evidence: Open issue since January with 13 comments indicating sustained community demand. Current workaround requires downloading .skill file, sending via Slack/Teams, and manual upload at Settings > Capabilities. User explicitly calls out the multi-step friction for teammates.

signals.topic: node -e inline execution corrupts CJK/non-ASCII document output
signals.summary: When Claude Code generates documents (e.g., .docx) with Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text using inline `node -e` calls, the shell mangles multi-byte UTF-8 sequences, resulting in garbled or `?`-substituted characters in the output file. The model eventually self-corrects by switching to file-based execution, but this costs extra token rounds on every occurrence — a predictable, avoidable failure.
aliases: CJK content corruption in document generation
non-ASCII text corruption in node -e execution
CJK font rendering missing from docx skill
signals.review_reason: User reports real output corruption in document generation — CJK characters are garbled in the final .docx file. This is not a theoretical concern; it is an observable failure in a specific, documented workflow. While the model eventually self-corrects, every such generation incurs avoidable extra token cost. The absence of a CJK font recommendation in the skill guidance also means users may not even realize the output is corrupted. This constitutes a repeated, predictable experience degradation for CJK-language users.

source_issues.title: node -e inline execution tends to corrupt CJK / non-ASCII content
source_issues.evidence: Body explicitly describes output corruption: shell mangles multi-byte UTF-8 before Node sees it, CJK content is garbled in final docx. Model self-corrects but only after extra token rounds. Secondary issue: even when bytes survive, CJK renders as boxes in Word without explicit font declaration (Arial has no CJK glyphs).

signals.topic: Account email address cannot be changed — users risk permanent loss of workspace/dev history
signals.summary: Claude accounts are permanently bound to their creation email address. Users who lose access to their corporate email domain (due to restructuring, migration, or business closure) are entirely locked out of their workspace with no recovery or migration path, losing hundreds of hours of project context and custom tool structures.
signals.review_reason: This is a single point of failure for any developer or organization whose corporate email domain becomes unavailable. Unlike minor friction, this results in permanent, irrecoverable loss of project history, custom tools, and billing records. The user explicitly quantifies the investment at 'hundreds of hours'. The fact that a competitor has already shipped this fix reinforces that this is a recognized gap, not an edge case. This meets the threshold for a real, high-impact user pain point despite only one issue being present in this snapshot.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request] Ability to change account email address to prevent workspace data loss - OpenAI/Codex added this feature already
source_issues.evidence: Body explicitly describes: no mechanism to change account email; if user loses corporate domain access (restructuring, migration, closure), they are 'entirely cut off' from development history with 'no migration path available'. Competitor (OpenAI/Codex) has already shipped this capability. User states they have invested 'hundreds of hours' building out Claude instances and custom tools — this is a direct, quantifiable asset at risk.

signals.topic: MCP server returns excessive data causing context window congestion
signals.summary: When using database-related MCP servers through Claude Code, returned data is not compressed or truncated, causing context window congestion and degrading the AI's ability to process the conversation effectively.
aliases: MCP data volume causes context overflow
signals.review_reason: Context window congestion from unfiltered MCP responses directly degrades the model's ability to function in data-heavy workflows (e.g., database operations). This is not a one-time cosmetic glitch — it actively impairs core functionality and forces users to work around the issue by manually limiting query scope. The presence of 2 comments indicates at least one other user has confirmed the problem.

source_issues.title: MCP returns excess data
source_issues.evidence: Body explicitly states: large data returns through MCP cause context congestion. User reports that claodecode obtained through MCP does not compress data, and when a database-related MCP is used, returning large amounts of data 'can cause congestion context'. 2 comments on the issue confirm the problem is reproducible.

signals.topic: No ability to share skills with hidden/proprietary instructions — IP exposure limits organizational adoption
signals.summary: When a skill is shared with teammates, recipients can view and copy all skill instructions. Users who have invested significant effort in crafting proprietary prompting logic have no way to share the capability without also exposing the underlying IP, limiting skill sharing to personal use cases only.
signals.review_reason: While framed as a feature request, this directly impacts organizational users who have built proprietary prompting workflows and cannot share them without full IP exposure. The blocking nature is real: the current sharing mechanism is functionally unusable for any organization that cares about instruction confidentiality. This is a structural gap rather than a missing convenience feature, making it a legitimate user pain point even at count=1.

source_issues.title: Feature Request: Skill sharing with hidden instructions
source_issues.evidence: Body explicitly states: shared skills are view-only but recipients can manually copy instructions into new skills they create. User cites 'proprietary workflows' and 'IP protection' as the blocking reason for organizational adoption of skill sharing. This is not hypothetical — the current design makes it impossible to share capability without sharing intellectual property.

signals.topic: DeepSeek v4-pro reasoning_content field incompatibility causing multi-turn API failures
signals.summary: Goose strips the `reasoning_content` field from assistant messages when sending multi-turn requests to DeepSeek v4-pro with thinking mode enabled. The DeepSeek API requires this field to be passed back verbatim, otherwise it rejects the request with HTTP 400. This breaks every tool-call conversation with this model on every turn after the first tool call.
aliases: deepseek-v4-pro reasoning_content must be passed back
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-blocking issue. DeepSeek v4-pro is a paid API model and every multi-turn tool-call conversation fails with HTTP 400, making the model entirely unusable for any real task. Evidence is explicit in both issue bodies showing API errors and root cause.

source_issues.title: Incompatible with DeepSeek v4-pro
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek v4-pro returns `reasoning_content` field but Goose does not handle it, causing incompatibility

source_issues.title: deepseek-v4-pro (thinking mode): multi-turn tool calls fail with 400
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 error: reasoning_content must be passed back to API on every tool-call turn; root cause is Goose stripping reasoning_content from assistant messages when constructing next API request

signals.topic: known_location() regression returns wrong region for Gemini 3.x models, causing silent API 404 failures on GCP Vertex AI
signals.summary: A regression introduced in PR #6393 causes `known_location()` to return Iowa (us-central1) for all Gemini variants including Gemini 3.x models. On GCP Vertex AI, Gemini 3.x only works with the global endpoint, not us-central1. Requests to us-central1 silently return 404, causing the model to produce zero tokens with no error surfaced to the user. Sessions appear active but no assistant response is ever generated.
aliases: Gemini 3.x models silent 404 on Vertex AI
wrong GCP region for Gemini 3 on Vertex AI
signals.review_reason: Gemini 3.x models are completely non-functional for GCP Vertex AI users. The model produces zero tokens and the session appears to hang, with no error surfaced. This is a silent failure that makes a major model family unusable. Two independent reports confirm the same regression.

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: Gemini 3.x models silently return 404 on Vertex AI with default config; us-central1 returns 404, global endpoint returns 200; fallback retry never fires because configured_location equals known_location

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: Self::Gemini(_) => GcpLocation::Iowa is wrong for gemini-3.x; fallback retry logic fails because both sides are Iowa; no error is surfaced to user

signals.topic: v1.34.0 GLIBC 2.38 requirement breaks startup on Ubuntu 22.04 and other stable Linux distributions
signals.summary: After the CI migration to Ubuntu 24.04 in PR #9075, the published v1.34.0 binary requires GLIBC 2.38 (Ubuntu 24.04). Users on Ubuntu 22.04 (GLIBC 2.35), Debian 12, RHEL 8, and RHEL 9 cannot start Goose v1.34.0 at all. The binary fails to load before main() runs with 'GLIBC_2.38 not found'. Users are forced to downgrade to v1.33.1 to recover.
aliases: GLIBC version mismatch after Ubuntu 24.04 CI migration
goose fails to start on Ubuntu 22.04
signals.review_reason: Full startup blockage for users on widely-used stable Linux distributions. The binary literally cannot start before main() runs, making Goose completely unusable for affected users. No workaround beyond downgrading. Explicit mention that Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, and RHEL 8/9 are all affected — all are actively supported OS versions.

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 requires libc6 2.38
source_issues.evidence: Binary fails with 'GLIBC_2.38 not found' before main() runs on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, RHEL 8/9; user forced to downgrade to v1.33.1

signals.topic: v1.34.0 Linux binary links libvulkan.so.1 unexpectedly, blocking startup for cloud-only inference users
signals.summary: The opt-in Vulkan feature was inadvertently compiled into the published Linux binaries via CI packaging paths. Users who run inference exclusively through cloud providers (e.g. AWS Bedrock) have no Vulkan loader installed, and the dynamic linker rejects the binary before main() runs with 'libvulkan.so.1: cannot open shared object file'. These users never touch local-inference code but are still blocked.
aliases: vulkan feature compiled into published artifacts
signals.review_reason: Binary fails to start before main() for a specific but real user segment (cloud inference users without Vulkan loader). The Vulkan feature was marketed as opt-in but was compiled into the published artifacts — this is a misleading packaging regression. Explicit user impact: startup is blocked with no workaround short of manually building without the feature.

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 published Linux binary requires libvulkan.so.1 at startup — not flagged in release notes
source_issues.evidence: Binary fails to start with 'libvulkan.so.1: cannot open shared object file' before main() for cloud-only inference users; not documented in release notes

signals.topic: Autovisualiser extension renders empty 'Waiting for data...' indefinitely — host-side regression in desktop app iframe message forwarding
signals.summary: The built-in Autovisualiser MCP extension shows an empty placeholder with 'Waiting for data...' for every chart type. MCP tool calls return valid structured data, but the desktop app host does not post the required `ui/notifications/tool-result` postMessage to embedded iframes after tool execution. This is a 100% reproducible regression affecting all chart types (chart, sankey, radar, donut, treemap, chord, map, mermaid) on every fresh restart.
aliases: Autovisualiser MCP extension visualization not rendering
iframe not receiving tool results postMessage
signals.review_reason: This is a regression affecting a built-in extension's core functionality. All visualization tools (8 chart types) fail to render, making the Autovisualiser extension completely unusable. The issue explicitly states it 'reproduces 100% across all autovisualiser tools on first use after a fresh app restart', indicating a persistent failure.

source_issues.title: The built-in Autovisualiser extension renders an empty placeholder showing 'Waiting for data...'
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible on every autovisualiser tool after fresh restart; MCP tool returns valid data but host does not post ui/notifications/tool-result postMessage to iframe

signals.topic: TypeScript 编译失败：使用 NodeNext 模块解析时因 `ai/dist` 未导出导致类型检查报错
signals.summary: 在 tsconfig 配置 NodeNext 模块解析并执行 `tsc --noEmit` 时，stagehand 包尝试解析 `ai/dist` 路径，但该路径未在 `ai` 包的 exports 中导出，导致构建失败。
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 明确描述了用户在使用标准 NodeNext TypeScript 配置时遇到的构建阻断问题：tsc 类型检查失败导致项目无法编译。这属于主流程阻断（build pipeline failure），有明确的用户影响证据（具体 tsconfig 配置 + ai 包版本），属于真实用户痛点而非纯功能请求。count=1 单仓问题降级为 P1。

source_issues.title: Failed `tsc` types with full check
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 NodeNext module resolution + noEmit 下构建项目时，stagehand 包的 index.d.ts 引用了 `ai/dist`，但该路径未在 ai@5.0.117 的 exports map 中导出，导致 TypeScript 类型检查失败，构建被阻断。

signals.topic: 上下文压缩后历史消息丢失且无法回补

aliases: 压缩后历史消息不可见
signals.review_reason: 上下文压缩后历史消息不可见是主流程阻断性问题：用户无法再查看已压缩的对话历史，且新对话页内无法回补更早消息。虽然底层数据未丢失（API 可访问），但前端访问能力丧失已构成用户可见的功能不可用。两条独立 issue 均提供了详细复现步骤和根因分析，证据充分。

source_issues.title: 新对话页发生上下文压缩后继续聊天，顶部无法继续加载更早历史消息
source_issues.evidence: 同一新对话页内连续多轮触发压缩后，滚动到顶部不会加载更早历史消息；但退出重进后又可加载。历史 run 消息实际未丢失（API 层面存在），但前端 UI 无法回补。

source_issues.title: 上下文压缩之后历史消息丢失

signals.topic: React 重复 key 警告影响消息列表渲染（v2.0 重现 v1 regression）
signals.summary: v2.0 前端消息列表渲染出现 React duplicate-key 警告，源于 mergeMessages 未去重以及 messages-tuple delta 累积导致同 id 消息出现两次。同类问题在 v1 中已被 #655 修复但未随 v2.0 重写迁移。
aliases: React duplicate key warning message list
signals.review_reason: React duplicate-key 警告是 UI 交互层面的明显体验下降：开发模式下每次对话产生大量控制台警告，Next.js DevTools 显示红标，影响调试体验。虽然不直接导致崩溃，但会导致 DevTools 问题面板不可用，且与 token-usage 渲染重叠相关。两条 issue 均提供了精确根因定位和可验证修复方案，置信度高。

signals.topic: 子代理上报 token 使用量时因回调对象类型错误导致异常退出

source_issues.title: [Bug] 子代理上报token使用情况时获取callback异常，导致子代理退出
