signals.review_reason: 每次启动重复认证直接损害CLI使用体验，是VS Code Extension和CLI之间的回归性差异，虽count=1但4条评论表明其他用户也受影响，用户影响显著。

source_issues.title: SSO session doesn't persist on each agent launch
source_issues.evidence: 用户每次退出并重新启动CLI终端会话均需重新SSO认证，VS Code Extension正常工作但CLI缺失该功能，有截图证据。4条评论表明其他用户也受影响。

signals.topic: Hardcoded legacy shell invocation breaks terminal commands on non-POSIX shells (tcsh, PowerShell Core)
signals.summary: Continue hardcodes '-l' flag for all Unix shells, which tcsh/csh do not support (exit code 1, 'Unknown option: -l'). On Windows, powershell.exe (PowerShell 5.1) is hardcoded instead of pwsh (PowerShell Core 6+), causing modern scripts using ternary operators, pipeline chain operators, and Unicode handling to fail unpredictably. Users cannot work around this as the shell invocation is deep in application logic.
signals.review_reason: Terminal command execution is a core workflow. Both issues share the same root cause: hardcoded shell assumptions that exclude valid, modern shell environments. tcsh issue blocks all terminal commands for affected users; PowerShell issue silently corrupts Unicode data and fails unpredictably on modern scripts. Two independent reports across different shells strengthen the pattern.

source_issues.title: Terminal commands fail when $SHELL is set to tcsh due to hardcoded -l shell flag
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: set $SHELL to /bin/tcsh, ask Continue to run any basic command. Error: 'Unknown option: -l'. Exit code 1. Every terminal command fails immediately.

source_issues.title: Hardcoded legacy Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe) causes runtime failures and degraded UX
source_issues.evidence: Modern PowerShell Core scripts fail with syntax errors (e.g., ternary operator '?', pipeline chain '&&'/'||'). Unicode silently corrupted by ASCII-only legacy PowerShell. Error messages are obscure and root cause (version mismatch) is difficult to diagnose. No user workaround as powershell.exe is hardcoded deep in application logic.

signals.topic: Markdown prompt files silently dropped when loaded via file:// URIs in config.yaml prompts section
signals.summary: When a markdown file is loaded via 'uses: file://prompts/xxx.md' in the prompts section of config.yaml, the unroll logic incorrectly wraps it in a 'rules' array instead of 'prompts', causing the content to be silently discarded. The debug log shows 'WARNING - Section "prompts" not found in resolved block config' but no user-facing error. This blocks users from using local prompt files in their config.
aliases: file:// URI prompt loading fails silently
prompts section markdown misidentified as rules
signals.review_reason: Config loading silently drops prompt content — users set up local prompt files but they are never applied. Root cause is in unroll.ts with verified debug evidence. Not P0 because count=1 and no evidence of widespread occurrence, but P1 is warranted as it completely defeats the intended config feature.

source_issues.title: Markdown Files in prompts Section are Misidentified as Rules and Dropped
source_issues.evidence: Root cause traced to unroll.ts: parseYamlOrMarkdownRule assumes all markdown files are rules and wraps in 'rules' array; calling loop expects 'prompts' key. Verified with debug logs: 'unrollBlocks: WARNING - Section "prompts" not found in resolved block config'. Content is silently dropped with no user-facing error.

signals.topic: Autocomplete falls back to non-existent 'AUTODETECT' model, causing repeated failures for custom provider users
signals.summary: Continue's autocomplete system repeatedly calls an 'AUTODETECT' model that does not exist in the user's provider configuration. Multiple Blablador users are affected, indicating this is a systemic issue rather than isolated. The autocomplete loop fails repeatedly, creating a degraded user experience and wasted API calls.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the reporter explicitly states 'Several Blablador users keep hitting this', indicating a real multi-user impact beyond a single report. Autocomplete failing repeatedly degrades the core editing experience and wastes API quota on failed calls. P1 is appropriate given the scope of user impact even with single-issue count.

source_issues.title: Continue keeps calling "AUTODETECT" model
source_issues.evidence: Author reports 'Several Blablador users keep hitting this.' Autocomplete system continuously attempts to call a model named 'AUTODETECT' that is not defined in any config. Causes repeated API failures on every autocomplete trigger.

signals.topic: JetBrains IDE autocomplete returns wrong suggestions on large files due to incorrect prefix/suffix extraction
signals.summary: On JetBrains IDEs, autocomplete on files over ~3000 lines produces entirely wrong suggestions. The prefix and suffix extracted from the file are incorrect and remain wrong regardless of cursor position. The same wrong suggestion persists across different cursor positions. This makes autocomplete unusable for any real codebase. The VS Code plugin does not exhibit this issue with the same config, isolating it to the JetBrains implementation.
aliases: JetBrains autocomplete wrong completions large files
signals.review_reason: Autocomplete is a primary feature of the tool. On JetBrains, the feature produces completely wrong output on large files — the model receives incorrect context, making completions meaningless. The user provides evidence from prompt.log comparing correct vs wrong behavior. Isolation to JetBrains implementation with working VS Code baseline rules out config/model issues.

source_issues.title: Truncated / wrong prefix & suffix on large file Autocompletion
source_issues.evidence: User provides prompt.log files showing correct prompt on small files but incorrect prefix/suffix on files over 3000 lines. Same wrong suggestion appears regardless of cursor position. VS Code plugin works correctly with identical config, isolating to JetBrains-specific code path.

signals.topic: Config parsing fails with opaque 'Invalid input' error, blocking extension load with no actionable guidance
signals.summary: When a user's config.yaml has a model definition issue (e.g., using ollama.com as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with incorrect model name), Continue fails to parse the config with 'Failed to parse config: models.0: Invalid input' — an error that provides no actionable information about what specifically is wrong or how to fix it. The extension fails to load, and the user is left with no path to resolution. This is a critical onboarding/blocking issue.
aliases: failed to parse config models.0 Invalid input
signals.review_reason: Extension load failure is a critical blocking issue that prevents users from using the tool at all. The error message 'Invalid input' is unacceptably opaque — it gives no indication of which field, value, or format is wrong, leaving users completely stuck. This is a P1 UX error message quality issue with a clear user impact: tool is unusable until resolved, and the resolution path is a mystery.

source_issues.title: Config error with ollama cloud
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'I have a config error, but nothing to tell me what is the error in the config. How do I know what the error is so I can fix it?' Full stack trace provided showing 'Failed to parse config: models.0: Invalid input' — error message gives no details about which field or value caused the failure. Extension fails to load. User filed this after being unable to find docs or guidance.

signals.topic: ValkeyStorage metadata_filter silently fails or errors - metadata-based memory retrieval is broken
signals.summary: ValkeyStorage's metadata_filter queries reference fields not indexed in the FT schema, causing queries to error or silently return wrong results for knowledge/memory retrieval.
aliases: valkey memory_index FT schema missing fields
signals.review_reason: Count is 2 deduplicated issues (#5795 and #5794) with the same root cause. This is a main flow failure: when users try to filter memory by metadata in ValkeyStorage, the filter either errors or silently returns incorrect results. The underlying storage layer silently fails, meaning agents may retrieve wrong memory entries without any error signal. This directly breaks knowledge retrieval which is a core crewAI feature.

source_issues.title: feat(valkey): metadata_filter fields not indexed in memory_index FT schema
source_issues.evidence: metadata_filter clauses in ValkeyStorage._vector_search() reference fields not in the FT schema. The memory_index only defines: VectorField embedding, TagField scope, TagField categories, NumericField created_at, NumericField importance. Custom metadata fields are not indexed. Result: queries will either error or silently return wrong results.

source_issues.title: feat(valkey): metadata_filter fields not indexed in memory_index FT schema
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #5795, same root cause. Raised during review of PR #5703. metadata_filter in ValkeyStorage queries fail because FT schema does not define those fields.

signals.topic: Tool retry causes duplicate side effects - payments/emails/trades re-executed without idempotency guard
signals.summary: When a task fails and retries, tool-decorated functions that already executed run again, causing duplicate side effects (payments, emails, trades) with direct financial/practical losses.
signals.review_reason: Clear main flow blocking issue with direct cost implications. When a task fails and retries, external API calls (payments, emails, trades) are re-executed without any deduplication guard. This is a confirmed bug with a concrete reproduction scenario—users experience real financial and practical losses. Referenced LangGraph Cloud issue confirms the pattern is known in production systems.

source_issues.title: Tool re-execution on task retry has no idempotency guard — duplicate payments, emails, trades possible
source_issues.evidence: When a task fails and retries, @tool decorated functions that already executed run again. Example given: stripe.charge() fires twice on retry. References LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 with same failure pattern in production. Fix requires durable external storage keyed before execution starts.

signals.topic: OpenAI API key works outside CrewAI but fails with 401 inside CrewAI due to environment variable isolation
signals.summary: API key validated successfully by tools but LLM calls fail with 401 AuthenticationError inside CrewAI, with VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch indicating subprocess environment isolation issue.
aliases: environment variable isolation breaks API auth
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking bug: users cannot run crews because API authentication fails inside crewAI even though the same key works outside. Tools validate successfully (suggesting key is visible at tool registration time) but LLM calls fail (suggesting key is lost or overridden at execution time via subprocess). The VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warning is a strong indicator of subprocess environment isolation issues. This prevents any user from running a basic crewAI workflow with OpenAI.

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: API key validated successfully via tools (INFO logs show 'Successfully validated tool') but actual LLM calls fail with 401. Full stack trace shows openai.AuthenticationError from completion.py. Virtual environment mismatch warning: VIRTUAL_ENV=/data/internal/venv does not match project environment /shared_venv. Same key works in curl and standalone Python. Issue includes detailed reproduction steps.

signals.topic: Claude 4.7 Opus model throws AnthropicException due to unsupported assistant message prefill
signals.summary: Users trying to use Claude 4.7 Opus get AnthropicException 'This model does not support assistant message prefill', blocking use of the latest Anthropic model.
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailability: users who want to use Claude 4.7 Opus cannot, as CrewAI throws an unhandled AnthropicException. While labeled as feature-request, the actual impact is a breaking exception for users trying to use the latest Anthropic model. The issue provides the specific error and root cause (assistant message prefill not supported by the new model).

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Support for new Anthropic model: Claude-4.7-Opus
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'AnthropicException - This model does not support assistant message prefill'. The new model removes temperature and uses adaptive thinking. The assistant message prefix ('Thought:') is not compatible. No workaround provided—users cannot use the newest Claude model.

signals.topic: VS Code extension UI lockup/scroll freeze caused by oversized globalState blocking main thread
signals.summary: Large chat history stored in VS Code's globalState API (~1.3 MB) causes the Extension Host to block the main thread via IPC serialization, resulting in complete UI lockup (scrolling, typing inoperable, Windows 'Window is not responding' prompt). Confirmed by CPU profiling and renderer logs. Root cause: globalState backed by in-memory SQLite not designed for large JSON blobs.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency (2 confirmed reports, multiple referenced in #27132) + main flow blocking (UI completely inoperable, Windows non-responsive prompt). CPU profile and renderer logs provide concrete evidence of root cause. Pattern recurs in every workspace during long sessions.

source_issues.title: VS Code UI lockup and Gemini lag: globalState storage blocking main thread
source_issues.evidence: CPU profiling shows extension host idle but renderer warns 'large extension state detected (1335kb)'. globalState backed by in-memory SQLite requires IPC pipe across main UI thread for every read/write. Complete UI lockup triggers Windows 'Window is not responding' prompt. Affects every workspace during long sessions or window reload.

source_issues.title: Cant scroll after certain amount of work
source_issues.evidence: User cannot scroll through terminal after extended use. Same root cause as #27132 — accumulated chat history overfilling globalState. Author explicitly notes 'I believe this issue might be the cause of #17933 and #27113' in #27132.

signals.topic: File editing failures: CLI unable to apply or parse code changes in editor
signals.summary: The agent prepares code changes in the side pane but consistently fails to apply them to the actual editor file, surfacing an error to the user. On Fedora, file editing fails even when the target content clearly exists in the file — suggesting parsing or file write failures.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct platforms (Windows/Fedora) with the same symptom — editing capability is broken and blocks the primary use case. Issue #27095 notes it 'never gets resolved' across recurring updates, indicating it is a persistent regression.

source_issues.title: Gemini code assist modifies the code on its side pane, but everytime it fails to apply the changes in the editor
source_issues.evidence: Recurring across multiple versions. Agent prepares changes in side pane but fails to apply them to the editor. Error dialog shown. User reports testing on 2-3 PCs with same result, confirming it's not OS/system-specific.

source_issues.title: [Fedora] Parsing and Editing errors
source_issues.evidence: CLI cannot edit files even when the target content exists. Screenshot shows error state. Platform: Fedora Linux. Confirmed by /about output showing version 0.42.0.

signals.topic: Auto-Edit mode ignores user-configured model, silently falls back to default flash model
signals.summary: When running in Auto-Edit mode, the CLI completely ignores the user's explicitly configured model (e.g., gemini-3.1-pro-preview) and silently falls back to the default flash model without any warning or error. This causes users to unexpectedly use lower-tier models for tasks they configured for premium models.
signals.review_reason: Clear user impact: users pay for premium models but the CLI silently downgrades them without notice. Config-driven behavior is silently overridden. Attached bug report with chat history JSON confirms root cause is internal hardcoded logic in Auto-Edit pipeline.

source_issues.title: Autoreuting
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with chat history JSON attached. Configured model 'gemini-3.1-pro-preview' is silently replaced with 'gemini-1.5-flash/2.0-flash'. No error or warning is raised. Identified as hardcoded restriction in Auto-Edit pipeline orchestration. Affects all users who configure non-default models.

signals.topic: macOS strict-open seatbelt sandbox blocks OAuth authentication, making CLI unusable
signals.summary: On macOS, when the strict-open seatbelt sandbox profile is enabled, the gemini-cli OAuth authentication flow fails completely — the CLI hangs at 'Waiting for authentication' and exits after ~2 seconds. The authentication cannot proceed regardless of sandboxAllowedPaths settings. This renders the CLI completely unusable for users requiring strict sandboxing.
signals.review_reason: Authentication is completely blocked when using the recommended strict-open security profile. This is a critical security/usability conflict: users must choose between strict sandboxing and being able to authenticate at all. The workaround requires downgrading security posture.

source_issues.title: [macOS] strict-open seatbelt profile blocks OAuth authentication flow
source_issues.evidence: CLI hangs at 'Waiting for authentication...' then exits after ~2s. Reproducible steps provided: configure strict-open profile, attempt OAuth. Workaround (switching to permissive-open) allows auth to proceed, confirming the strict-open profile is the blocker. Related to issue #19275 but remains unresolved.

signals.topic: ~/.gemini/.env environment file not loaded in untrusted workspace folders, causing endless OAuth login loop
signals.summary: When running gemini-cli in a directory classified as untrusted, the CLI does not load ~/.gemini/.env, which contains required environment variables (e.g., GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT). As a result, authentication credentials are treated as invalid and the user is trapped in an endless login loop with no way to authenticate without switching to a trusted directory.
signals.review_reason: Complete auth flow is broken for users in untrusted directories. The .env file (a standard configuration mechanism) is silently ignored, leading to an endless login loop — a user-experience anti-pattern that provides no diagnostic information.

source_issues.title: ~/.gemini/.env VS untrusted folder
source_issues.evidence: User requires GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT in .env for workspace accounts. CLI loads .env in trusted folders but silently skips it in untrusted folders, making credentials invalid and causing an infinite authentication loop. No error message is shown to explain why auth fails.

signals.topic: Windows users cannot install smolagents[dev] via uv due to mlx[cpu] having no Windows wheels
signals.summary: When Windows users attempt `uv pip install -e "smolagents[dev] @ ."`, uv's dependency resolver fails because the mlx[cpu] extra dependency has no win_amd64 wheels. This blocks the entire local development setup flow for all Windows contributors/users.
aliases: mlx[cpu] platform tag missing on Windows
smolagents[dev] dependency resolution fails on Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-blocking issue. Windows users cannot complete local dev setup via the documented uv installation command, which is a core workflow. The issue is labelled 'bug' and provides clear reproduction steps on two Python versions.

source_issues.title: BUG:  No solution found when resolving dependencies while uv
source_issues.evidence: Windows user attempted `uv pip install -e "smolagents[dev] @ ."` on both Python 3.11 and 3.12 environments. uv reports: 'Because mlx[cpu] has no wheels with a matching platform tag (e.g., win_amd64) and smolagents[dev]==1.25.0.dev0 depends on mlx[cpu], we can conclude that smolagents[dev]==1.25.0.dev0 cannot be used.'

signals.topic: SerializationError shows literal '{e}' instead of actual exception details due to f-string double-brace escape bug
signals.summary: In serialization.py line 429, the f-string uses double braces `{{e}}` which renders as literal `{e}` in error output instead of interpolating the exception object. Users whose pickle serialization fails see the uninformative string 'Cannot serialize object: {e}' with no actionable details.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed code bug with explicit root cause. When pickle serialization fails, the error message becomes opaque, preventing users from diagnosing the underlying issue. The fix is trivial (change {{e}} to {e}) but the impact on debuggability is real.

source_issues.title: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message
source_issues.evidence: Code at serialization.py line 429 raises SerializationError with f"Cannot serialize object: {{e}}" — double braces produce literal '{e}' in output rather than interpolating the exception. User sees 'Cannot serialize object: {e}' instead of actual exception message, making debugging impossible.

signals.topic: SubAgent response_format causes malformed ask_human arguments in intermediate tool calls
signals.summary: When a declarative SubAgent has response_format configured, intermediate tool calls (specifically ask_human/HITL approval) produce malformed structured arguments — summary becomes null and option objects become empty {}, breaking human-in-the-loop approval flows. Without response_format the same tool calls work correctly.
aliases: SubAgent response_format breaks intermediate tool calls
SubAgent HITL approval broken by response_format
signals.review_reason: Confirmed user-impacting bug: response_format on SubAgents corrupts intermediate ask_human structured arguments, breaking human-in-the-loop approval flows. Explicit before/after diff in bug report shows fields become null/empty. Non-trivial edge case requiring code-level fix — not a configuration issue.

source_issues.title: SubAgent response_format affects intermediate tool/HITL calls
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with minimal reproducible example. Expected ask_human structured_data has full fields (summary.total=2, options with value/label); with response_format added, summary becomes null and options become [{},{}]. Process exits 0 without raising, but behavioral output is incorrect — blocks the approval/HITL workflow for any user relying on structured SubAgents.

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.ls silently swallows FileNotFoundError/PermissionError, returning empty LsResult and poisoning agent context
signals.summary: BaseSandbox.ls catches FileNotFoundError and PermissionError with bare pass, returns LsResult(entries=[]) identical to a legitimately empty directory. Agents cannot distinguish missing paths from empty directories, leading to false context, wrong reasoning, and inability to self-reflect — resulting in incorrect final answers.
aliases: ls command returns empty result for non-existent paths without error
LsResult error field never populated on path errors
signals.review_reason: Confirmed user-impacting bug: silent error suppression in sandbox ls causes agents to receive false empty-directory context, directly leading to wrong answers and broken self-reflection. User explicitly describes 'context poisoned with false information' as the outcome. Clear behavioral regression from expected error-reporting consistency with other Result types.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.ls silently swallows FileNotFoundError/PermissionError, returning empty LsResult on invalid paths
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with clear description: 'This causes my agent's context to be poisoned with false information, therefore not able to self-reflect properly and give the correct answer to the final user.' Agents silently proceed on wrong path assumptions. LsResult.error field exists but never populated. Consistent with GrepResult/GlobResult/ReadResult which correctly set error on failure.

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware IndexError crash when LLM returns empty messages list
signals.summary: SubAgentMiddleware crashes with IndexError at subagents.py line 411 because result['messages'][-1] is accessed without checking if the list is empty. Occurs when LLM (e.g. Anthropic Claude) emits a zero-output end_turn turn after completing a task, causing complete process failure for any agent using SubAgentMiddleware with such models.
aliases: IndexError in SubAgentMiddleware on empty LLM response
SubAgent crash when messages list is empty
subagents.py line 411 IndexError on zero-output AIMessage
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash bug: IndexError in SubAgentMiddleware directly blocks the subagent execution path, causing process failure. Explicit Python traceback location (subagents.py line 411) and reproducible condition (empty messages list). Affects any user running SubAgentMiddleware with models that emit zero-output end_turn turns.

source_issues.title: IndexError in SubAgentMiddleware when LLM returns empty messages
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction steps. IndexError at subagents.py line 411 — direct crash that blocks the subagent execution path. Related issues #3043 and #3044 referenced. Fix identified as one-line guard: check if not result['messages'] before accessing [-1]. Confirmed on latest main branch.

signals.topic: Trailing empty AIMessage causes SubAgent to return empty ToolMessage to parent, producing wrong answers
signals.summary: Anthropic Claude (Bedrock) occasionally emits a trailing end_turn AIMessage with zero output tokens after a successful final tool call (e.g. write_todos). The subagent's task-tool extractor only looks at messages[-1].text, so the parent receives an empty string instead of the actual answer, leading to wrong final output.
aliases: SubAgent returns empty response when LLM emits trailing end_turn
Empty AIMessage causes parent to receive blank tool result
write_todos trailing message causes subagent answer loss
signals.review_reason: Confirmed user-impacting bug: trailing empty AIMessage from Anthropic Claude causes subagent to silently lose its actual answer, returning empty string to the parent agent — resulting in wrong output. Specific message sequence documented. Users running Claude via Bedrock in subagent workflows are affected whenever the model emits a zero-output end_turn after a final tool call.

source_issues.title: Fall back to the last non-empty AIMessage for subagents
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with concrete message sequence example showing [-3] AIMessage with real answer, [-2] ToolMessage from write_todos, [-1] AIMessage empty with output_tokens=0. Parent agent receives blank string as subagent result. Proposed fix walks reversed messages to find last non-empty AIMessage. Related issue #1022.

signals.topic: stream_events(v3): reasoning content silently dropped from persisted AIMessage when message also contains tool_call
signals.summary: When using stream_events(version="v3") with models that emit reasoning blocks followed by tool_calls in the same message (e.g. Gemini with thinking enabled), the reasoning text is silently lost from the assembled AIMessage.content. The reasoning is visible during streaming via the .reasoning projection, but the persisted message — what gets checkpointed, returned from nodes, and shown on conversation read-back — has reasoning gone. This breaks agent conversation history and context for all tool-calling turns.
aliases: reasoning content missing from AIMessage content with tool_call
gemini reasoning dropped from persisted message
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：所有使用 stream_events(v3) + 带思考能力模型（如 Gemini）的 agent 在遇到 tool_call 时，其对话历史中的 reasoning content 被静默丢失。streaming 过程中可见但 checkpoint/持久化后消失，导致 agent 的多轮对话上下文缺失。这直接影响基于 agent 的生产应用的核心状态管理功能，阻断用户的主流程。两条独立 issue 确认同一根因，且提供了精确的代码定位。

source_issues.title: stream_events(version="v3"): reasoning content dropped from AIMessage when message also contains a tool_call
source_issues.evidence: Root cause in langchain_core/language_models/chat_model_stream.py _finish: _sweep_chunk_store handles tool_call_chunks but has no equivalent sweep for _reasoning_per_block. When provider emits content-block-delta for reasoning but no terminating content-block-finish before the next block, reasoning never lands in self._blocks. Confirmed on Gemini 2.5/3.x with thinking enabled. Persisted AIMessage has content=[{type:tool_call}] only — reasoning is gone from content, additional_kwargs, and response_metadata.

source_issues.title: stream_events(version="v3"): reasoning content dropped from AIMessage when same message contains a tool_call
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #37420. Minimal repro provided using langchain_core.language_models.chat_model_stream.ChatModelStream dispatch API. Confirms that .reasoning projection exposes reasoning during stream but _assemble_message does not include it. Affects any agent using stream_events v3 with reasoner models.

signals.topic: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound multi-turn requests, causing agent loops to fail with HTTP 400
signals.summary: ChatDeepSeek._create_chat_result captures reasoning_content from API responses into AIMessage.additional_kwargs, but the outbound path inherited from BaseChatOpenAI._get_request_payload drops it when serializing assistant messages back to the API. DeepSeek reasoner models require the prior turn's reasoning_content to be echoed back on each multi-turn request, and reject the call with HTTP 400. Single-shot invoke() works, but any agent loop (create_react_agent, create_agent) breaks on the second turn.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：使用 DeepSeek reasoner 模型的 agent 在多轮对话（任何涉及 tool 调用的场景）时，第二轮请求直接抛出 HTTP 400 错误导致 agent 循环崩溃。两条 issue 均提供完整复现代码和精确根因定位（outbound payload 序列化路径缺少 reasoning_content）。这是 langchain-deepseek 包的核心功能回归，直接破坏 agent 循环可用性。

source_issues.title: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound requests, breaking multi-turn / tool-using flows with reasoner models
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 error: 'The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.' Affects create_react_agent / create_agent in LangGraph. Root cause: _get_request_payload serializes messages to API but drops additional_kwargs['reasoning_content']. Complete reproduction with @tool and agent.invoke provided. Fix proposed: override _get_request_payload to mirror reasoning_content onto outbound dict.

source_issues.title: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound requests, breaking multi-turn / tool-using flows with reasoner models
source_issues.evidence: Confirms same root cause as #37390: ChatDeepSeek._create_chat_result captures reasoning_content inbound but outbound path (inherited from BaseChatOpenAI._get_request_payload via _convert_message_to_dict) silently drops it. Affects all reasoner models. DeepSeek API documentation confirms multi-round requirement.

signals.topic: ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(...).stream() drops response headers / x-request-id, breaking observability
signals.summary: When using ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream(), the streamed AIMessageChunk / final message objects do not contain HTTP response headers (specifically x-request-id) inside response_metadata. This makes it impossible to correlate streamed requests with provider-side logs and incidents. The same flow works correctly for non-structured streaming and AzureChatOpenAI structured streaming.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：使用 ChatOpenAI structured output + streaming 的用户在生产环境中无法将请求与 provider 端日志关联，x-request-id 完全丢失。无可用 workaround，必须依赖 provider 侧手动匹配。影响 langchain + langchain-core + langchain-openai 三个包的核心功能路径。虽然是单条 issue，但提供了完整可运行的复现代码和对比测试，证据充分。

source_issues.title: ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream() drops response headers / x-request-id in response_metadata
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction with HeaderCaptureHandler callback shows x-request-id present for plain streaming (A) but missing for with_structured_output+json_schema streaming (B). Root cause in the structured output streaming path — different code path than non-structured streaming. Impacts production observability: users cannot correlate streamed requests with provider-side logs.

signals.topic: Chroma.update_document() raises ValueError when Document metadata is omitted, inconsistent with add_documents()
signals.summary: Chroma.update_document() raises ValueError: 'Expected metadata to be a non-empty dict, got 0 metadata attributes in update.' when passed a Document without explicitly provided metadata. In contrast, Chroma.add_documents() accepts the same Document(page_content='...') without metadata. This API inconsistency forces users to explicitly pass metadata={} to update_document, or causes unexpected failures when updating documents that were originally added without metadata.
aliases: Chroma metadata inconsistency add vs update
signals.review_reason: 体验下降（API 不一致）：Chroma 的 add_documents 和 update_document 对同一 Document 结构的处理行为不一致，update 路径强制要求 metadata 存在，导致用户代码在更新原始无 metadata 文档时静默失败。虽然是单仓问题（langchain-chroma），但影响向量存储的核心 CRUD 操作，用户无法写出同时兼容 add/update 的通用代码。

source_issues.title: `Chroma.update_document()` fails when `Document` metadata is omitted
source_issues.evidence: Complete reproduction: add_documents(Document(page_content='Original')) works, update_document(document_id='doc_1', document=Document(page_content='Updated')) raises ValueError. Root cause: langchain_chroma/vectorstores.py update_documents passes document.metadata directly without normalizing None to {}. Provides possible fix: metadata = [document.metadata or {} for document in documents].

signals.topic: grep_search Python fallback silently skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() using default cp1252 encoding
signals.summary: On Windows, when ripgrep is unavailable or disabled and FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware.grep_search falls back to _python_search(), it calls file_path.read_text() without an encoding parameter. On Windows this defaults to cp1252, causing valid UTF-8 text files to raise UnicodeDecodeError and be silently skipped. This makes grep_search unreliable on Windows — searches may return incomplete or empty results even when matching content exists in normal UTF-8 files.
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败：grep_search 在 Windows 上存在静默数据丢失——UTF-8 编码的文件被静默跳过，搜索结果不完整但没有任何错误提示。用户可能误以为搜索范围正确而遗漏关键结果。这是 langchain agent 文件搜索中间件的平台特定 bug，直接影响 Windows 用户的生产使用。

source_issues.title: grep_search: Python fallback skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() encoding
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: _python_search() calls file_path.read_text() with no encoding parameter; on Windows default is cp1252 not UTF-8. UnicodeDecodeError is caught and file is silently skipped via 'except (UnicodeDecodeError, PermissionError): continue'. Fix proposed: use explicit UTF-8 encoding. Platform-specific but significant for Windows users.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud — 2-3x cost impact
signals.summary: When tool calls exceed ~3 minutes on LangGraph Cloud, the system silently re-dispatches them from checkpoint while the original is still running, completing both and creating 2-3x redundant work and cost. Multiple mitigation attempts (BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS, BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS, asyncio.to_thread wrapping) all failed. Root cause traced to hardcoded BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120s and sweep interval of 240s causing cancelled runs to be re-queued.
signals.review_reason: P0: Extremely strong user impact evidence — 2-3x direct cost impact confirmed by source-level tracing, reproducible across multiple versions and cloud tiers, all attempted mitigations failed. This is a cost-bleed bug silently multiplying API costs for agents doing long-running tool calls, a common production pattern.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed duplicate runs with identical content hash appearing at ~180s intervals; original and duplicate both complete successfully; pattern reproducible across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6, EU Cloud, Plus tier; multiple env-var mitigation attempts failed; source traced to hardcoded heartbeat and sweep logic in langgraph-api

signals.topic: Interrupt() in a loop causes extra resumes — node executes extra times on retry
signals.summary: Using interrupt() inside a while loop causes nodes to be re-executed extra times on subsequent resumes, even when valid data is provided. Each graph.invoke(Command(resume=valid_value)) after an interrupt in a loop triggers an extra node invocation beyond what the loop logic warrants, corrupting agent state and wasting LLM API calls.
signals.review_reason: P0: interrupt() is a core HITL primitive. Extra executions on retry directly corrupt agent state and waste LLM calls. Although count=1, the explicit bug label + self-contained reproducible example + core HITL workflow impact (not edge-case) justifies P0.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Interrupt() in a loop will cause extra resumes
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with minimal code: interrupt() inside while True loop, then graph.invoke(Command(resume=valid_value)) called multiple times — each invocation causes extra node runs beyond expected single retry

signals.topic: invoke(v2) returns polymorphic types inconsistently — list[StreamPart] vs GraphOutput undocumented
signals.summary: Calling graph.invoke(..., version='v2') with stream_mode != 'values' returns list[StreamPart] instead of GraphOutput, which is undocumented. 6 linked prior issues (#7008, #4796, #4028, #2870, #5932, #4355) show this is a recurring pain point. The polymorphic return type breaks type-checking, causes runtime errors for code expecting dict-like output, and creates confusion between v1 and v2 behavior.
signals.review_reason: P1: Main API (invoke v2) has undocumented polymorphic return — users cannot rely on type-checking and get runtime errors. 6 linked prior issues confirms this is a recurring pain point. No cost or cloud dependency so P1 not P0.

source_issues.title: invoke(version="v2") returns list[StreamPart] instead of GraphOutput when stream_mode != "values" — polymorphic return type undocumented
source_issues.evidence: 6 linked prior issues (#7008, #4796, #4028, #2870, #5932, #4355) all on the same topic; explicit bug label; reproducible minimal example; polymorphic return type causes runtime failures for code expecting consistent dict output

signals.topic: InMemoryStore search filters treat dotted keys as literal top-level keys instead of nested paths
signals.summary: InMemoryStore.search() with filter={'user.access-level': 'value'} treats 'user.access-level' as a literal top-level key rather than a nested path (user -> access-level). Dot-notation in filter keys silently returns empty results instead of performing the intended nested search, making the API counterintuitive and error-prone for nested data.
aliases: nested filter key not working in InMemoryStore
signals.review_reason: P1: Data store search returning silently empty results is a significant user pain point — queries fail silently rather than with an error, making bugs hard to detect. Verified on main branch with minimal reproducible code.

source_issues.title: InMemoryStore search filters treat dotted keys as literal top-level keys instead of nested paths
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 2-line code: filter={'user.access-level': 'nested'} returns [] while filter={'user': {'access-level': 'nested'}} returns correct results; behavior is counterintuitive — dot-notation is a common convention for nested paths

signals.topic: draw_graph: TypeError when sorting edges with None data from conditional edges
signals.summary: Calling graph.get_graph() on a StateGraph that has a node returning Command[Literal[...]] AND uses add_conditional_edges from the same node raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str'. This crashes graph visualization for a common graph pattern involving conditional edges combined with Command returns. Affects versions 1.1.10 through 1.2.0a5.
aliases: sorted() fails on NamedTuple with None data field
signals.review_reason: P1: graph.get_graph() is a core debugging and visualization tool — a TypeError crash means users cannot inspect their graph structure at all when using this common pattern. Blocks the primary debugging workflow for affected graph topologies.

source_issues.title: draw_graph: TypeError sorting edges with None data from conditional edges
source_issues.evidence: Explicit TypeError crash in draw_graph(); reproducible with node using Command[Literal[...]] + add_conditional_edges; affects versions 1.1.10 through 1.2.0a5; root cause in sorted() on NamedTuple with str|None data field

signals.topic: Plugin upgrade silently breaks existing workflow tool nodes (references old version hash, no error raised)
signals.summary: When a plugin is upgraded, existing workflow tool nodes retain stale version hashes in DSL and fail silently with no output. Downstream nodes receive empty values. No error is raised despite broken tool resolution.
aliases: Plugin version hash not updated on upgrade
Plugin upgrade breaks workflow tool references
signals.review_reason: User-impacting silent failure: plugin upgrade permanently breaks all workflows using that plugin without raising any error. User loses output data with no indication of failure cause. Severity is high because it affects production workflows without any warning.

source_issues.title: Plugin upgrade does not update existing workflow plugin_unique_identifier references, causing silent tool failure
source_issues.evidence: Plugin upgraded from bowenliang123/md_exporter v2.1.0 to v3.6.9; existing workflow tool nodes still reference old hash; workflow executes without error but tool node produces no output; downstream answer nodes receive empty values; root cause is DSL plugin_unique_identifier not updated on plugin upgrade

signals.topic: LLM node fails with 'Invalid upload file' error in text-only chat flows with no file uploaded
signals.summary: LLM node in text chat flows occasionally throws RuntimeError 'Invalid upload file' even when no file was uploaded. The ABORT strategy terminates the workflow with a confusing error message unrelated to the actual user action.
aliases: LLM node ABORT with 'Invalid upload file' in text-only flow
RuntimeError Invalid upload file without file upload
signals.review_reason: Intermittent workflow failure with a misleading error message that has no relation to user action (text-only chat). The ABORT strategy terminates the workflow, blocking the user's main use case. The false 'Invalid upload file' error message confuses users about root cause.

source_issues.title: Node llm failed with ABORT strategy: Invalid upload file
source_issues.evidence: User asks question in text format via API; LLM node intermittently fails with 'Node llm failed with ABORT strategy: Invalid upload file' followed by 'RuntimeError: Invalid upload file'; no file was uploaded; workflow is completely blocked by misleading error

signals.topic: Workflow run status remains 'running' after termination, never reaches terminal state
signals.summary: After a user terminates a workflow run, the status remains 'running' indefinitely instead of transitioning to stopped/failed. Both Cloud and self-hosted v1.14.1 affected.
aliases: Workflow termination does not update run status
Terminated workflow stays in running state
signals.review_reason: Workflow termination control is broken across both Cloud and self-hosted deployments. Users cannot trust the workflow control mechanism, leading to confusion about actual run state and potential resource waste.

source_issues.title: Workflow run remains running after being terminated in v1.14.1
source_issues.evidence: Both Dify Cloud and self-hosted v1.14.1; after running a workflow and terminating, the run status stays 'running' indefinitely instead of 'stopped' or 'failed'; user cannot confirm if termination succeeded; evidence via video recording

signals.topic: LLM node fails with 'invalid file' error when processing knowledge retrieval results containing _source field
signals.summary: LLM node in workflow fails with 'invalid file' when knowledge results retrieved via HTTP contain the _source field. This is a regression; workflow previously worked. Removing _source fixes the error but breaks Dify's citation feature.
aliases: HTTP knowledge results _source field causes LLM node to fail
LLM node invalid file error with knowledge citation data
signals.review_reason: Regression blocking knowledge retrieval + LLM workflow execution. Users who rely on HTTP-retrieved knowledge results (common for distributed Dify deployments) cannot use this combination. Citation feature is also broken as a workaround. Clear user impact with specific trigger path.

source_issues.title: LLM node failing with 'Invalid File' message

signals.topic: Dataset metadata field names invisible when adding documents to dataset
signals.summary: When adding metadata fields to a dataset and then adding a document, the metadata field names are not displayed in the UI. Users cannot see what metadata fields they are filling in.
aliases: Metadata field labels not visible in document upload UI
Dataset metadata field names not displayed
signals.review_reason: UI rendering issue blocks users from understanding what metadata they are filling in during document upload. While not a complete block, it directly prevents users from populating dataset metadata correctly, a core data ingestion workflow.

source_issues.title: The meta data field names are invisible when I adding them to a document
source_issues.evidence: User adds metadata fields to dataset, then adds a document; metadata field names are not visible in the UI when adding the document; blocks correct data entry into metadata fields

signals.topic: Graph Memory poisoning via user-injected content — attacker-controlled facts persisted as trusted memory and served to other users
signals.summary: In shared Graph Memory (Neo4j/Memgraph), a normal untrusted user message can be transformed into persistent graph-memory evidence that is merged into existing entity neighborhoods and later retrieved as trusted context for different users. No privileged access required — only normal UI interaction. Demonstrated with a healthcare scenario where attacker-injected drug contraindication overrides factual medical information.
signals.review_reason: Issue #5151 is a confirmed security disclosure with a full PoC showing a normal user injecting drug contraindication facts into shared Graph Memory that are later retrieved by the victim agent as trusted context — directly leads to harmful real-world outcomes (wrong medication). #5127 independently confirms missing authorization on a related memory config endpoint allowing global config hijack. #5130 reinforces the same attack surface (memory poisoning / ASI06). All three are open and unfixed as of the snapshot date. The attack requires no privileged access and affects multi-user shared-memory deployments in healthcare, finance, and policy-support domains — a clear primary flow block.

signals.topic: POST /configure missing role-based authorization — any API key holder can redirect all LLM and embedder traffic to attacker-controlled endpoint
signals.summary: The /configure endpoint validates authentication token but never checks the caller's role. Any distributed API key can change the global LLM provider URL and API key, redirecting all user prompts, memories, and embeddings to an attacker-controlled server. Configuration persists in PostgreSQL and survives restarts. Full 6/6 PoC demonstrates data exfiltration.
aliases: global LLM config takeover via API key
signals.review_reason: Issue #5127 contains a complete end-to-end PoC with 6/6 tests passing against a real Mem0 Docker deployment. The /configure endpoint accepts any valid API key and modifies the global LLM/embedder configuration, allowing traffic redirection. The PoC explicitly captures a user password (Sup3rS3cret) being sent to the attacker-controlled endpoint. The User.role field exists but is never checked in verify_auth(). This is a primary flow block — every user on an affected Mem0 instance is exposed to prompt/memory exfiltration if any single API key is compromised.

signals.topic: memory.add() crashes with 400 Bad Request when conversation exceeds embedding model token limit (8192 tokens) — entire memory storage flow blocked
signals.summary: Phase 1 (existing memory retrieval) embeds the full raw conversation into a single vector before extracting facts. If the conversation exceeds the embedding model's 8192-token limit, the call fails with openai.BadRequestError and no memory is stored or retrieved. Reproduction shows a multi-turn conversation with ~40 messages triggering the crash. Even when under the limit, multi-topic conversations produce poor recall.
aliases: embedding 400 Bad Request on long conversations
memory add fails at token limit
conversation length causes memory storage crash
signals.review_reason: Issue #5148 provides a full reproduction with exact error traceback (openai.BadRequestError 400, 'maximum input length is 8192 tokens') and a concrete 40-message conversation example. The crash occurs in the primary memory.add() flow before any memory extraction or storage happens, completely blocking the user from storing any memories. This is a confirmed primary flow block with a clear traceback and reproducible steps.

signals.topic: @mem0/openclaw-mem0 npm package ships unbuilt TypeScript — prevents OpenClaw gateway from starting on all recent OpenClaw versions
signals.summary: The published npm package has no dist/ directory, no main/module fields in package.json, and no build scripts. Recent OpenClaw versions (2026.4.30+) hard-require compiled ./dist/index.{js,mjs,cjs} from installed plugins. Installing the plugin now causes the gateway to fail to start with a non-recoverable error. openclaw doctor --fix does not auto-build and provides no real remediation.
signals.review_reason: Issue #5106 documents a clear packaging bug: the published npm package contains only raw TypeScript source with no build output. This causes the OpenClaw gateway to fail to start entirely on any current OpenClaw installation (2026.4.30+). Users must manually run npx tsdown to build the plugin, and the workaround must be re-run after every reinstall. This is a confirmed packaging/release issue that renders the plugin completely non-functional for all users of current OpenClaw versions.

signals.topic: pgvector psycopg ConnectionPool causes DNS resolution failures and extended hangs in Docker production environments
signals.summary: In Docker Compose production environments, the psycopg ConnectionPool for pgvector intermittently fails with 'failed to resolve host' DNS errors despite DNS working at the OS and Python level. Pool creation hangs for 30+ seconds during ASGI lifespan startup, and repeated failures cause resource exhaustion that can crash the container. Direct psycopg.connect() with the same parameters works fine. Django's psycopg pool works in the same container. Only affects Docker Compose production deployments.
aliases: pgvector connection pool hangs in Docker
pgvector pool initialization blocks application startup
signals.review_reason: Issue #3950 is a confirmed bug with specific environment details (Docker Compose, pgvector/pgvector:pg18, psycopg3), multiple reproduction observations, and a clear hypothesis about the interaction between psycopg pool initialization and Docker's internal DNS resolver. The bug causes application startup hangs (30+ seconds) and can lead to resource exhaustion requiring container reboot — a significant availability impact in production. The fact that Django's psycopg pool works in the same container confirms this is a mem0-specific issue.

signals.topic: .NET AG UI session stops updating after first turn in multi-turn workflow
signals.summary: When using AGUIChatClient in a multi-turn workflow, the session stops updating after the first agent invocation. Subsequent agent calls using the same session do not update the session state, despite the backend using in-memory session store.
aliases: AG UI session not updating after first turn
AG UI multi-turn session state loss
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker for multi-turn AG UI workflows. The issue describes a reproducible blocking behavior where the session stops updating after the first turn, which directly prevents the core multi-turn conversation loop from functioning. The 'reproduced' label confirms this is a confirmed bug affecting the primary interaction pattern.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: AG UI session stops updating after first turn
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly describes the main multi-turn workflow being blocked: 'session no longer updated' after the first agent invocation. Backend uses in-memory session store with no restarts, yet subsequent calls in a while(true) monitor loop fail to update the session. Labeled 'reproduced' by maintainers.

signals.topic: MCP server unreachable: incorrect exception type raised, breaking user error handling
signals.summary: When an MCP HTTP server is unreachable, agent-framework raises an unhandled ExceptionGroup wrapping ConnectError instead of the expected ToolException. This prevents users from catching the error with their own exception handlers and breaks expected error-handling workflows.
aliases: MCP server unreachable exception type wrong
MCP connect failure raises ExceptionGroup instead of ToolException
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker for MCP error handling. When an MCP server goes down, users cannot catch the exception with their own handlers — their try/except block is bypassed entirely. This breaks the expected error-handling contract and forces users into complex internal exception management. Clear user impact: own exception handler is ineffective.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Incorrect exception raised while MCP server is unreachable
source_issues.evidence: User provides exact reproduction code showing `except Exception as e` block is bypassed by the bug. Error thrown: `Error: ('Failed to enter context manager.', ExceptionGroup('unhandled errors in a TaskGroup', [ConnectError('All connection attempts failed')]))`. The issue explicitly states 'the error is not handled due to the bug', directly breaking user error-handling code paths. Labeled 'reproduced'.

signals.topic: Python DevUI streaming memory growth regression: >10GB consumption causing browser kill
signals.summary: In Python release 1.3.0, a regression reintroduces the DevUI streaming memory growth issue. Streaming responses accumulate in memory without release, consuming over 10GB and causing the browser process to be killed.
aliases: browser killed by memory growth in DevUI streaming
signals.review_reason: This is a main dev-loop blocker. DevUI is the primary local development and debugging tool for agent-framework. A regression that causes >10GB memory consumption and browser kill directly blocks the core development workflow. The explicit 'regression' framing and reference to prior issue #5221 confirms this is a confirmed, recurring defect with significant user impact.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Regression on DevUI streaming memory growth issue
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly described as a regression from version 1.3.0 that causes >10GB memory consumption and browser process kill. References previous issue #5221 for more detail. DevUI is the primary local development and debugging tool — blocking this breaks the main dev loop. Labeled 'reproduced'.

signals.topic: propagate_session=True breaks sub-agent when using Responses API: service_session_id conflict causes 400 errors
signals.summary: When using agent.as_tool(propagate_session=True), the child agent inherits the parent's service_session_id. After the parent's first LLM call, MAF auto-populates this from the Responses API's conversation_id, and the child sends it as previous_response_id — which the server rejects with a 400 'No tool output found' error because the parent's tool_call is still pending. Additionally corrupts OpenTelemetry trace hierarchy.
aliases: as_tool propagate_session causes service_session_id conflict with Responses API
signals.review_reason: This is a primary multi-agent workflow blocker. The as_tool(propagate_session=True) pattern is a key capability for composing sub-agents. The 400 error completely breaks this pattern with the default Responses API. The issue provides exact error messages from Application Insights telemetry and a clear reproduction case — user impact is unambiguous. No reliable workaround exists without custom middleware.

source_issues.title: Python: propagate_session=True breaks sub-agent when using Responses API (service_session_id conflict)
source_issues.evidence: Provides exact error from Application Insights: `openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'No tool output found for function call call_yqKQ1r87I0HNWcXRxpkoqrJA', 'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}`. Demonstrates with reproduction code that any `as_tool(propagate_session=True)` usage fails with the Responses API. Also documents telemetry corruption (orphaned spans) from exception propagation.

signals.topic: A2A streaming handler emits duplicate messageId and empty Parts arrays, causing client rejection
signals.summary: The A2A streaming handler (HandleNewMessageStreamingAsync) emits one Message per streaming chunk. Many chunks have empty convertible content, producing Parts=[] arrays that violate the A2A spec (REQUIRED non-empty). All chunks share the same messageId from the underlying OpenAI completion ID, causing A2A clients to collapse the stream to a single (often empty) message. The only working workaround is disabling streaming entirely.
aliases: A2A streaming Message with empty Parts array
A2A streaming client rejection due to spec violation
signals.review_reason: A2A streaming is a key framework capability. The bug causes spec-violating messages that are rejected by compliant A2A clients (Python a2a-sdk), effectively breaking A2A streaming end-to-end. The workaround of disabling streaming is a significant UX regression. Assigned P1 (not P0) because the workaround (disable streaming) exists, though it loses the primary feature value. Confidence is high due to exact client-side validation errors documented.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: A2A streaming handler emits one Message Per chat-client update with shared messageId and empty Parts on bookend chunks
source_issues.evidence: Provides exact Python a2a-sdk pydantic validation error: 'Message object must have a non-empty parts array.' Also shows collapsed empty message from duplicate messageId. Workaround requires disabling streaming capability entirely on the agent card, which is not a viable production solution. A2A streaming is a primary feature of the agent framework.

signals.topic: GroupChat round-robin speaker selection skips last agent when max_round is an even number (off-by-one error)
signals.summary: GroupChat's round-robin algorithm skips the last agent when max_round is set to an even number. With 3 agents and max_round=4, agent C never speaks. Root cause is an off-by-one error in the speaker selection loop.
aliases: GroupChat agent C never speaks even max_round
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed logic bug that disrupts the main workflow of GroupChat — a core AutoGen feature. The round-robin scheduling is fundamentally broken for even max_round values, meaning the last agent in the group is systematically excluded from participation. While count=2 (two duplicate reports), both are confirmed closed bugs with reproducible steps. This qualifies as P1 because it is a non-blocking but significant workflow failure affecting a core feature, not an edge-case configuration.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed reproducible: Create GroupChat with agents A, B, C; set max_round=4; observe agent C is never selected. Root cause: off-by-one error in speaker selection loop. autogen-agentchat 0.4.x on Python 3.11.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report of same bug by same author on same day, independently confirmed. Identical reproduction steps: 3 agents, max_round=4, agent C never speaks. Confirms bug is not an isolated incident.

signals.topic: AutoGen Studio default-auth RCE via WebSocket FunctionTool.exec() — CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated arbitrary code execution
signals.summary: AutoGen Studio WebSocket endpoint accepts unauthenticated team_config payloads; FunctionTool._from_config() directly calls exec() on attacker-controlled source_code, enabling unauthenticated RCE on default deployments. No authentication, no sandbox, no input validation.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed critical security vulnerability with direct user impact: unauthenticated RCE on default AutoGen Studio deployments. The attack chain is fully documented, requires zero prerequisites, and achieves full server compromise. The default configuration has authentication disabled, making every public-facing AutoGen Studio instance exploitable. This meets the P0 bar of '主流程阻断 + 高频场景' — it blocks the entire AutoGen Studio deployment from being used securely without immediate patching.

source_issues.title: [Security] Critical: Unauthenticated RCE via WebSocket team_config (CVSS 9.8)
source_issues.evidence: CVSS 9.8 Critical. Unauthenticated remote code execution via WebSocket team_config payload. FunctionTool._from_config() directly executes attacker-controlled source_code via exec() with no sanitization, no sandbox, and default AuthConfig type='none'. Works on default AutoGen Studio v0.4+ Docker deployment. No user interaction required.

signals.topic: openai.BadRequestError when using Gemini models for tool calls in autogen-agentchat
signals.summary: Using Gemini 1.5 Pro with autogen-agentchat 0.4.1 and google-generativeai 0.8.0 causes openai.BadRequestError during tool call execution. The tool call flow is blocked for Gemini model users.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug that blocks the tool call workflow for Gemini model users. Tool calling is a core AutoGen feature, and the BadRequestError prevents the main execution flow from completing when using Gemini models. This is user-impacting and clearly reported with environment details and reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: openai.BadRequestError when using Gemini models for tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed: autogen-agentchat 0.4.1 + google-generativeai 0.8.0 + Gemini 1.5 Pro causes openai.BadRequestError during tool call execution. Error is specific to Gemini models; other models work without this error. Issue was closed after triage.

signals.topic: http_client property missing in serialized model config, blocking custom corporate model endpoints

Users with corporate custom model endpoints requiring specific HTTP client settings (e.g., custom TLS verification) cannot use autogen-ext with their infrastructure.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed configuration limitation that blocks users from using autogen-ext with custom corporate model endpoints. The inability to serialize http_client through YAML/JSON config forces users to maintain out-of-band configuration, breaking reproducible deployments. This has been an open issue since November 2025 with ongoing community engagement, indicating real user pain rather than an edge case.

source_issues.title: Add http client property in serialized config
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed: When using a company's customized model endpoint, if http_client is not passed, the endpoint rejects access. Users must load serialized config from YAML/JSON but cannot include http_client in the serialized format. signals.topic: Codegen generates setInputFiles() without absolute file path, causing test failures when run from different working directory
signals.summary: When recording file input operations with codegen, the generated setInputFiles() call only contains the filename without any path. Running the generated test from a different directory causes the file to not be found, breaking the recorded test.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: The arguments for setInputFiles() generated by codegen do not include the file path.

signals.topic: Codegen generates redundant click() before setInputFiles() for <input type="file"> elements, leaving file dialog open

signals.review_reason: The redundant click() generates a native file dialog that setInputFiles() cannot close, causing the generated test to hang or fail when executed. This is a direct test execution blocker produced by codegen's own recording logic.

signals.topic: @playwright/mcp misattributes missing ffmpeg as missing browser, misleading users on root cause
signals.summary: When ffmpeg is the missing executable (e.g., for recordVideo), @playwright/mcp throws 'Browser chrome is not installed' instead of naming ffmpeg. Users run the wrong install command and waste time diagnosing the real cause.
signals.review_reason: Users receive a completely wrong diagnostic message and are directed to install a browser that is already installed. This causes significant wasted time and confusion, and the workaround requires users to manually identify the actual missing dependency.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @playwright/m reports "Browser "chrome" is not installed" when ffmpeg is actually the missing executable
source_issues.evidence: Chrome is installed and resolves correctly. Running 'npx playwright install ffmpeg' fixes the MCP invocation. The error rethrow path in browserFactory.ts unconditionally names the browser channel instead of the actual missing executable.

signals.topic: Codegen 'Assert text' popover textarea has unreadable text in dark mode due to forced text color
signals.summary: The codegen 'Assert text' tool displays a textarea popover with forced light-mode text color on dark backgrounds, making text unreadable when the system uses dark mode.
signals.review_reason: The codegen Assert text tool is unusable in dark mode as the textarea text is visually inaccessible. While not a test execution blocker, it prevents users from using a core codegen feature on dark-mode systems.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Unreadable text in textarea.text-editor under dark mode due to forced text color
source_issues.evidence: Codegen Assert text tool shows textarea with text color too close to dark background. User provided screenshots showing unreadable white-on-white text. Root cause traced to forced text color in highlight.css.

signals.topic: Playwright reporter silently drops AggregateError.errors[] sub-errors, hiding critical failure details
signals.summary: When tests throw AggregateError (e.g., in fixture teardown), only the top-level message is shown in the reporter. The errors[] array containing the actual sub-error details is silently dropped, severely degrading debugging capability.
signals.review_reason: AggregateError is commonly thrown in fixture teardown when cleaning up multiple resources. Losing the sub-errors array means users cannot see which specific teardown operations failed, making debugging test cleanup failures extremely difficult.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `AggregateError.errors[]` sub-errors are invisible in reporter output — only the top-level message is serialized
source_issues.evidence: filterStackTrace in util.ts recurses through e.cause but never walks e.errors[]. AggregateError is the idiomatic pattern for surfacing multiple failures from teardown and Promise.allSettled. All sub-error details are silently dropped in reporter output.

signals.topic: JSON serializer options mismatch causes enum parameters to fail in kernel function calls
signals.summary: KernelJsonSchemaBuilder uses JsonStringEnumConverter for tool schema, but KernelFunctionFromMethod.TryToDeserializeValue uses default JSON options, causing System.ArgumentException at runtime when any kernel function has enum parameters
aliases: JsonStringEnumConverter mismatch between schema and deserialization
signals.review_reason: 运行时阻断：任何含枚举参数的 kernel function 在工具调用时都会因序列化选项不一致而崩溃，属于主流程失败。提供了完整复现步骤和堆栈证据。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: JSON serializer options don't match between tool schema and tool calls, causing enum parameters to fail.
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: define a tool with enum parameters, invoke it, and get System.ArgumentException + System.Text.Json.JsonException. Stack trace shows failure in KernelFunctionFromMethod.Invoke with type conversion error on enum. Known TODO comment in codebase acknowledges the mismatch.

signals.topic: Missing NuGet package version blocks PgVector connector upgrade
signals.summary: PgVector connector v1.75.0 (containing VectorSearchOptions fix) is unavailable on NuGet Gallery, forcing users to stay on broken v1.74.0
signals.review_reason: 用户无法在 NuGet Gallery 获取修复版本，导致 PgVector connector 的 VectorSearchOptions bug 无法通过升级解决，属于关键 connector 不可用的阻塞问题。

source_issues.title: .Net: Missing version on Nuget Gallery for Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector
source_issues.evidence: User reports being unable to upgrade to v1.75.0 where VectorSearchOptions bug is fixed, because that version is missing from NuGet Gallery. User is blocked on v1.74.0.

signals.topic: Codex mobile shows running desktop as offline and Reconnect silently does nothing — remote connection status completely broken
signals.summary: Codex mobile/Codex Web show a running desktop as offline, and the Reconnect action does nothing (no loading state, no error, no retry). Users cannot connect to Codex from mobile at all.
aliases: Codex Web remote desktop shows offline
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but thematically linked issues confirm a consistent remote connection status failure: (1) running desktop appears offline with Reconnect silently failing — blocking the primary remote access use case with zero error feedback; (2) stale ghost connection records cannot be removed. Combined they make the mobile remote Codex integration unusable and give users no diagnostic path. This is a clear session-state problem causing key functionality breakdown.

source_issues.title: Codex mobile shows running desktop as offline and Reconnect silently does nothing
source_issues.evidence: Desktop app is open and running, but mobile shows 'Offline · Last seen 18 hours ago'. Tapping Reconnect produces no loading state, no error, no retry indication. Mobile app remains stuck. Key remote feature completely unusable with zero user feedback on failure.

source_issues.title: Codex mobile : Stale codex mobile connections
source_issues.evidence: Codex mobile shows ghost/stale synced connection records (codex-remote-1, codex-remote-2) as Offline with 'last seen' timestamps. No delete or remove option exists for these entries. User cannot clear stale records.

signals.topic: Remote context compaction fails — workflow blocked on long sessions
signals.summary: Context compaction fails with context_length_exceeded or 502 Bad Gateway errors, preventing users from continuing long Codex sessions via mobile/Web control.
signals.review_reason: Two separate authors report compaction failures via the same remote compact endpoint — one with context_length_exceeded (code bug) and one with 502 Bad Gateway (infrastructure bug). Both block the same critical workflow: continuing a long Codex session. Users cannot proceed past context limits, defeating the purpose of the session. Strong user impact evidence from both.

source_issues.title: Codex Web remote compaction fails with context_length_exceeded from mobile session
source_issues.evidence: User tapped 'Please keep going' in a long mobile-controlled Codex session; compaction triggered but returned raw context_length_exceeded error instead of resuming. Session cannot continue. UI showed 'Compacting context' then error with no recovery path.

source_issues.title: 502s on compaction
source_issues.evidence: Error running remote compact task: unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway at https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses/compact. Long sessions fail compaction, preventing continuation. Error returned via Cloudflare.

signals.topic: Codex agent stops before goal is complete — main coding workflow interrupted
signals.summary: Codex acknowledges the goal is not complete but stops prematurely for an unspecified internal reason, leaving user work unfinished.
signals.review_reason: Agent stops mid-goal with explicit UI acknowledgment that the task was not completed. This is a primary workflow blocker: users invoke Codex to accomplish coding tasks, and when it stops before finishing without a clear reason, the core value proposition fails. Clear user-visible evidence in the issue body and screenshot.

source_issues.title: Codex stopping before goal is complete
source_issues.evidence: Codex stops before the goal is complete, explicitly acknowledging in the UI that the goal is not complete, but stops anyway. Screenshot shows Codex displaying that the task was not finished. User uploaded thread 019e21cb-7ecd-7b72-9243-f7ad4f095aab. Main agent workflow is interrupted mid-task.

signals.topic: Codex Desktop crashes on launch on macOS 26.4 — app completely unusable
signals.summary: Codex Desktop crashes immediately on launch (EXC_BREAKPOINT/SIGTRAP in Electron startup) before any UI or login screen appears.
signals.review_reason: App crashes immediately on launch with a trace trap in the Electron startup chain, before any user interaction is possible. This is a complete startup crash — the entire application is unusable. Strong evidence with full crash report and diagnostic attachments. Despite count=1, the impact is total app unavailability, warranting P1.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop 26.513.20950 (2816) crashes on launch on macOS 26.4 build 25E5218f with EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP in Electron Framework / V8 / Node startup
source_issues.evidence: Codex Desktop exits immediately with EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP) during Electron Framework/V8/Node startup. Crash occurs before any UI or login screen renders. Incident Identifier 3E25A905-8342-4126-89BE-5EA28D7E47B. User tried rebooting, re-launching, re-installing, and diagnostic collection without resolution. App is completely unusable.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox runner error (CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5) — skills fail to load on Windows
signals.summary: Windows sandbox fails with permission error (CreateProcessAsUserW: 5) every first attempt, causing skill retrieval failures.
signals.review_reason: A consistent Windows sandbox permission error breaks skill loading on every Codex invocation. Skills are a core feature, and failure on first attempt means users must retry or work around broken behavior on every interaction. Error code 5 (Access Denied) indicates a Windows-level permission problem in the sandbox runner.

source_issues.title: windows sandbox: runner error: CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, Codex always fails on first attempt to retrieve skills with error: 'windows sandbox: runner error: CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5'. This is a Windows permission error affecting the sandbox runner. Affects every prompt (not a one-off). Business account, gpt-5.5 xhigh fast model. Skills are central to Codex functionality and fail consistently on every Windows invocation.

signals.topic: AdvancedSQLiteSession data integrity — silent failures and orphaned data in session persistence
signals.summary: AdvancedSQLiteSession suffers three related data integrity bugs: add_items() reports success after structure metadata write failure (messages silently unreadable), delete_branch() leaves orphaned messages in the base table, and OpenAIConversationsSession persists empty reasoning items that the API rejects. All three cause session state to become inconsistent or corrupt with no error surfaced to the caller.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed bugs across the same session persistence subsystem with clear data-integrity impact: messages saved but unreadable (3348), orphaned rows causing DB bloat (3346), and session persistence hard failure with API rejection (3268). All three are silent failures that corrupt or block the session state without surfacing errors to the caller.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.add_items can report success after structure metadata failure
source_issues.evidence: add_items() commits base rows then silently swallows structure metadata write failure. Callers observe success but get_items() cannot read the saved messages.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.delete_branch() leaves branch-only messages in the base table
source_issues.evidence: delete_branch() removes metadata rows but leaves underlying agent_messages rows orphaned. Database grows with invisible data.

source_issues.title: OpenAIConversationsSession persists empty reasoning item and Conversations API rejects it
source_issues.evidence: SDK persists {"type":"reasoning","summary":[]} which the Conversations API rejects as 'Invalid item' during session persistence. This is a hard failure in the session persistence flow.

signals.topic: Realtime approval — rejection reasons dropped and unqualified tool lookup keys cause inconsistent approval state
signals.summary: Two interrelated Realtime approval bugs: (1) local on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but it is dropped and replaced with a generic HITL rejection message, preventing the model from seeing specific rejection context; (2) approval-state reuse uses bare tool names while the rejection path already uses qualified tool lookup keys, causing approval lookups to fail for namespaced or synthetic tools.
signals.review_reason: Two bugs in the same Realtime approval subsystem: (1) rejection reasons are information-loss bugs that degrade the model's contextual awareness in human-in-the-loop flows; (2) qualified vs. bare name inconsistency causes approval lookups to silently misfire for namespaced tools. Both affect the critical approval gating mechanism.

source_issues.title: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped
source_issues.evidence: Local tool on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but that reason is dropped and replaced with a generic HITL rejection message. The model receives no specific rejection context.

source_issues.title: Realtime approvals should use qualified tool lookup keys
source_issues.evidence: Approval-state reuse checks bare tool name while rejection path already uses qualified tool_lookup_key. For namespaced or synthetic tools, approval lookups will fail to match the correct tool.

signals.topic: Realtime known-tool branch — exceptions propagate without model-visible tool output, breaking agent loop
signals.summary: In the Realtime tool execution path, the known-tool branch (_handle_tool_call 'if' branch at line 697) calls invoke_function_tool() without try/except. Any exception (ToolTimeoutError, ValueError, etc.) propagates out of the handler with no tool output sent to the model, leaving the conversation in an inconsistent state where the model never receives feedback about the failure.
