signals.review_reason: Core Realtime flow is broken: the known-tool exception branch has no error handling, causing tool failures to escape without any model-visible output. This directly breaks the Realtime agent loop for any tool that raises an exception — a primary workflow failure in the Realtime subsystem.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output
source_issues.evidence: The known-tool 'if' branch at line 697 has no try/except around invoke_function_tool(). Exceptions propagate out with no RealtimeModelSendToolOutput sent, leaving the model with no feedback and the conversation in an inconsistent state.

signals.topic: Chat Completions converter sends empty tool output for non-text results, silently hiding tool output from the model
signals.summary: Converter.items_to_messages() converts non-text tool output content to an empty array (content: []) when preserve_tool_output_all_content=False. This silently hides meaningful image/audio/file tool results from the model in the next turn, with no error or warning to the caller.
aliases: Chat Completions converter non-text tool output empty
signals.review_reason: Tool output containing meaningful non-text content (images, audio, files) is silently replaced with an empty message, making the next model turn receive no feedback about the tool result. This is silent data loss in the agent loop with no error surfaced to the caller.

source_issues.title: Chat Completions converter can send empty tool output for non-text results
source_issues.evidence: Converter.items_to_messages() converts non-text function_call_output to content: [] silently. The next model turn receives an empty tool message, and debugging is misleading since no error is surfaced.

signals.topic: Voice text splitter silently drops non-empty custom chunks shorter than 20 characters
signals.summary: StreamedAudioResult drops text chunks returned by a custom TTS text_splitter when the chunk is non-empty but shorter than 20 characters. This causes short voice responses (e.g., 'ok') to be silently omitted even when the custom splitter explicitly marked the text as ready for TTS.
aliases: Voice custom TTS short chunk dropped
TTS text splitter drops short responses
signals.review_reason: Voice output is silently truncated for short responses when using a custom TTS text splitter. The user gets no feedback that 'ok' or similar short responses were dropped, causing incomplete voice output in a user-facing streaming feature.

source_issues.title: Voice text splitter drops short custom chunks
source_issues.evidence: StreamedAudioResult drops non-empty custom splitter chunks shorter than 20 chars. Short responses like 'ok' are silently omitted despite the splitter explicitly marking the text as TTS-ready.

signals.topic: Streaming `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when duplicate indexes appear in first chunk, producing unparseable JSON
signals.summary: When a streaming chunk contains two `tool_calls` entries with the same `index`, `accumulate_delta` stores them as separate list elements instead of merging by index, leaving orphaned entries and mangled function arguments that fail JSON parsing. Triggers with speculative decoding (vLLM, Kimi 2.6) but is a library-level logic bug independent of model/backend.
aliases: streaming tool_calls duplicate index accumulation bug
tool_calls fragments dropped on duplicate index in first chunk
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: tool_call 是 Agent/Realtime 工作流的核心能力，streaming delta 合并错误直接导致 tool_calls.function.arguments 无法被 JSON 解析，Agent 工具调用完全失败。同时影响 vLLM、Kimi 等 OpenAI-compatible server 用户，波及 speculative decoding 场景。两条独立 issue 均提供可复现代码，复现路径明确。

source_issues.title: `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when one chunk has multiple entries at the same `index`
source_issues.evidence: When first chunk contains two tool_calls entries with index=0, accumulate_delta stores list wholesale instead of merging by index. Resulting arguments JSON is unparseable. Reproduced with vLLM speculative decoding, openai v2.35.0.

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: accumulate_delta assumes physical list position equals index field, ignoring the index field on first chunk. Causes orphaned second duplicate-index entry with mangled function.arguments that produces invalid JSON. Reproduced with Kimi 2.6 on vLLM. 7 comments, active discussion.

signals.topic: Responses API multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing `response.output` back as `input` via `model_dump()`
signals.summary: Passing response.output items back as input via model_dump() on reasoning models produces a 400 'Unknown parameter: input[1].status' because model_dump() fabricates null fields (status, encrypted_content) that the API rejects. Additionally, an undocumented pairing constraint requires reasoning+message to be consecutive, breaking multi-turn history management across multiple downstream projects.
aliases: multi-turn response output as input 400 error
model_dump fabricating null fields causing API rejection
signals.review_reason: 核心对话流程阻断: multi-turn 是 Responses API 的基础使用模式，turn 2 必然失败导致多轮对话无法实现。影响 OpenClaw（64.9k forks）生产环境，同时影响 agents-python SDK 和 pydantic-ai 等下游库，波及面极广。根因明确（model_dump 空字段 + API 校验），有可复现代码，workaround 不优雅（previous_response_id 无法替代手动历史管理需求）。

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() fabricates status:None and encrypted_content:None for fields API never returned; API rejects null unknown parameters with 400. OpenClaw (64.9k forks) broken in production, plus agents-python SDK and pydantic-ai downstream. Issue #3009 (pairing constraint) is same root cause. Workaround is previous_response_id but breaks manual history management.

signals.topic: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM)
signals.summary: In v2.34.0, passing empty string to api_key raises 'Missing credentials' error due to new credential validation logic, breaking compatibility with local OpenAI-compatible servers that intentionally pass api_key="". Previously worked in v2.33.0 and all earlier versions.
aliases: empty api_key credential validation regression v2.34.0
local server compatibility broken by credential check
signals.review_reason: 本地开发/部署阻断: 大量开发者使用 openai-python 连接本地 LLM 服务器（vLLM、llama.cpp 等），api_key="" 是标准做法。v2.34.0 升级后所有本地 server 全部失效，属于回归性阻断。尽管有 workaround（传占位符），但对用户来说行为突变且需要改代码，不适合 P0（count=1、无多源证据）。

source_issues.title: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
source_issues.evidence: New credential validation in _client.py (v2.34.0) checks 'not self.api_key' (falsy for ''), causing OpenAIError. Local servers (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM) intentionally pass api_key='' because no auth needed. This worked in v2.33.0 and all prior versions. No auth-free server can be used without workaround (api_key='not-needed').

signals.topic: `summary="auto"` produces no reasoning summary events on codex model variants during Responses API streaming
signals.summary: When calling the Responses API with reasoning={"effort": "high", "summary": "auto"} and stream=True on gpt-5.3-codex (and gpt-5.1-codex variants), the SDK never emits response.reasoning_summary_part.added / response.reasoning_summary_text.delta / response.reasoning_summary_part.done events. The stream goes straight to output_text.delta with no summary in between. The same code works reliably on gpt-5-mini.
aliases: reasoning summary events not emitted on codex models streaming
streaming reasoning summary missing for codex model variants
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用: reasoning summary 是 codex 代码任务流的显式用户请求功能（用户主动设置 summary='auto'），但该功能在 codex 模型上完全不工作，属于 API 行为与用户预期严重不符。虽然 count=1，但 streaming reasoning 能力是 model 产品差异化的关键功能，值得 P1 而非降为 P2。

source_issues.title: `summary="auto"` produces no reasoning summary events on `gpt-5.3-codex` (Responses API, streaming)
source_issues.evidence: SDK confirmed as issue (checkboxed). On codex variants streaming with reasoning summary='auto', zero reasoning_summary events emitted. Same calling code on gpt-5-mini emits events reliably. Reproduced on gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-5.1-codex-max. Active issue with maintainer response.

signals.topic: Realtime API does not execute tool calls when using MCP server
signals.summary: When using the Realtime API with MCP tools, the model never executes tool calls despite successfully receiving instructions and MCP connection. Logs only show the initial instruction message, and tool calls are never triggered. Tested with working MCP via @modelcontextprotocol/inspector.
aliases: realtime MCP tool execution not happening
realtime API MCP tools not called
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用: MCP tool execution 是 Realtime API 的核心能力，用户已通过独立工具验证 MCP 连接正常，但 SDK+Realtime 层完全无法触发 tool calls，属于主流程阻断。当前标注 P1 因 count=1 且 MCP Realtime 属于早期功能，无多源证据支撑 P0。

source_issues.title: Realtime does not execute tool calls with mcp
source_issues.evidence: Connected realtime SIP app with Twilio via Azure Realtime API. MCP confirmed working via @modelcontextprotocol/inspector. Logs only show instruction intro message; tool calls never fire. Library issue confirmed (checkboxed). Active thread with 2 comments, recently active.

signals.topic: create_triage_agent function missing from swarm.agents module — documented example code fails to import
signals.summary: The function `create_triage_agent` is referenced in `examples/personal_shopper/main.py` as `from swarm.agents import create_triage_agent`, but no `agents.py` file exists under the `swarm/` folder, causing the import to fail and blocking users from running the example.
aliases: agents.py not found in swarm package
example code import error for create_triage_agent
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue: the provided example in `examples/personal_shopper/main.py` references a non-existent module `swarm.agents.create_triage_agent`. Users attempting to run the official example encounter an ImportError immediately, which constitutes a startup crash and blocks the primary onboarding flow. No workaround is documented.

source_issues.title: no create_triage_agent
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'from swarm.agents import create_triage_agent; no agents.py under the folder swarm'. The import fails at runtime because the referenced module does not exist, blocking execution of the provided example.

signals.topic: Session history API does not reflect live assistant/tool events during active turn — blocks real-time orchestration polling
signals.summary: When Codex is actively running, `acpx <agent> sessions history` only shows the user prompt entry. Assistant text and tool-call entries are not checkpointed into session history until the turn finishes, even though those events are already available in the underlying Codex rollout JSONL on disk. This forces orchestrators to parse the rollout log directly instead of using the natural `sessions history` API for live progress monitoring.
signals.review_reason: Real-time progress monitoring via session history API is broken during active turns. Orchestrators cannot poll `sessions history` for live updates and must fall back to directly parsing the rollout log. Clear user impact for any programmatic/acpx-as-orchestration-layer workflow.

source_issues.title: ACP session history only records prompts while Codex is running
source_issues.evidence: During a live Codex session, `sessions history` shows only the user prompt while assistant/tool events are absent, even though the rollout JSONL on disk already contains them. The `agentSessionId` field also remains `-` while the turn is in flight, making programmatic tailing unreliable.

signals.topic: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while direct acpx claude succeeds — blocks automated two-agent workflows
signals.summary: OpenClaw's `/acp spawn claude` command fails with `ACP_TURN_FAILED / UNAVAILABLE / Internal error`, while the same Claude agent works fine when invoked directly via `acpx claude`. This blocks the automatic Codex + Claude two-agent ACP flow that depends on OpenClaw's spawn mechanism.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow path is blocked: OpenClaw's spawn mechanism for Claude ACP fails with a generic internal error while the direct path works. Automated two-agent orchestration flow is completely broken. Clear user impact with no timeout or auth workaround available.

source_issues.title: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while direct acpx claude succeeds
source_issues.evidence: Direct `acpx claude` succeeds from the same host, Gateway is stable, auth is fine, but OpenClaw `/acp spawn claude` fails with `ACP_TURN_FAILED / UNAVAILABLE / Internal error`. The automatic two-agent ACP flow (Codex + Claude) is blocked as a result.

signals.topic: Claude ACP runtime config options (timeoutSeconds, thinking) cause ACP_TURN_FAILED — users forced to bare-prompt-only workaround
signals.summary: When OpenClaw applies standard runtime controls as ACP `session/set_config_option` calls (e.g., `timeoutSeconds`, `thinking: "medium"`), the Claude ACP adapter rejects them with `AcpRuntimeError: Internal error`. Only clean prompts and model overrides work. Users must fall back to bare-prompt-only workflows, losing standard operational controls.
signals.review_reason: Standard runtime controls (timeout, reasoning effort) cause Claude ACP to crash with internal error, forcing users to use bare-prompt-only workflows. Loss of operational controls is a significant UX regression for production use. The adapter does not advertise which config options it supports, leading to opaque failures.

source_issues.title: Claude ACP config option handling: generic runtime controls fail while clean/model-only path works
source_issues.evidence: Smoke test matrix shows `timeoutSeconds: 180` fails, `thinking: "medium"` fails, `thinking: "high"` fails, and even `model: "sonnet" + thinking: "high"` fails — all with `AcpRuntimeError: Internal error`. Only clean prompts and standalone model overrides succeed. The issue reproduces across multiple OpenClaw stack versions.

signals.topic: Third-party plugins ingest attacker-controllable external data into agent context and perform authenticated mutations, enabling prompt injection attacks across 11 plugins
signals.summary: Eleven ClawHub plugins (supalytics, algorithm-solver, tester, reposit, betbud, sentry-observability, aster, gog, sunday, vnsh, web-scraper) ingest unsanitized data from external sources (analytics UTM/referrer fields, crypto tweets, GitHub issues/PRs, community solutions, web HTML) into the agent context and drive authenticated mutation actions, enabling indirect prompt injection with real destructive impact.
aliases: prompt injection via external data ingestion in plugins
agent context injection leading to authenticated mutations
indirect prompt injection from external data sources in plugins
signals.review_reason: These 11 plugins all share the same root cause: ingesting unsanitized external data into the agent context and using it to drive authenticated mutation actions. The impact is not merely theoretical — each plugin maps attacker-controllable fields (UTM, tweets, GitHub issues, community text, emails, analytics data) to real destructive authenticated actions (delete products, send emails, execute shell, create blockchain markets, manage vault credentials). Users who install any of these 11 plugins are exposed to indirect prompt injection with concrete harm vectors, not just data exfiltration.

source_issues.title: Security: yogesharc/supalytics returns raw visitor-controlled analytics fields (UTM, referrer, page) into agent context, exposing authenticated supalytics sites mutations
source_issues.evidence: Supalytics skill ingests visitor-controllable UTM/referrer/page fields and uses agent context to drive authenticated 'supalytics sites add/update/remove' mutations. External attacker can poison analytics fields to steer agent into unauthorized site management actions.

source_issues.title: Security: wd1993/algorithm-solver feeds attacker-suppliable problem statements into code-generation, then executes the generated Python via Bash
source_issues.evidence: Algorithm-solver ingests arbitrary problem text and generates Python code that is executed via Bash tool. Attacker-supplied LeetCode/interview-style problem text can embed hidden directives shaping generated code, which is then executed under the agent's Bash authority.

source_issues.title: Security: tsiontesfayechromaway/tester pipes raw GitHub issue and PR review content into authenticated gh-driven sub-agent workflow, exposing repository mutations
source_issues.evidence: GitHub tester ingests raw gh issue/PR comment content and uses it to drive 'gh pr comment' and sub-agent actions under the user's authenticated gh authority. Attacker can plant prompt injection in GitHub issue/comment text to trigger unauthorized repository mutations.

source_issues.title: Security: tomasz-tomczyk/reposit pulls community-submitted solutions into the coding agent context on proactive search, exposing coding-agent tool authority
source_issues.evidence: Reposit proactively searches community knowledge base on errors and feeds results into the coding agent with file-read/edit/Bash authority. Attacker can submit malicious 'solutions' to target common errors, causing the agent to exfiltrate secrets or run arbitrary shell commands.

source_issues.title: Security: steipete/gog ingests raw Google Workspace content (Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Sheets/Docs) into agent context, exposing authenticated cross-product mutations
source_issues.evidence: gog plugin ingests Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, and Docs content under broad OAuth scope and exposes authenticated mutations (email send, calendar write, file upload) to the agent. Attacker can send a targeted email with injection text or manipulate a calendar invite to steer the agent into unauthorized Google Workspace actions.

source_issues.title: Security: sergical/sentry-observability prints raw Sentry issue/event/log telemetry into agent context, exposing authenticated Sentry CLI actions during incident investigation
source_issues.evidence: Sentry-observability ingests raw Sentry telemetry (issue titles, event data, logs) into agent context with authenticated Sentry CLI mutations available. Attacker can create a Sentry event with injection text to steer agent into unauthorized Sentry event deletion or other mutations.

source_issues.title: Security: seanwyngaard/web-scraper-as-a-service feeds attacker-controlled target-page HTML into code-generation, then executes the generated python scraper locally
source_issues.evidence: Web-scraper-as-a-service allows specification of arbitrary target URLs and feeds the returned HTML into LLM code generation, which is then executed locally via Bash. Attacker-controlled pages can inject directives into generated code executed under the agent's Bash authority.

source_issues.title: Security: satyajiit/aster forwards raw Android SMS and notification text into the AI agent webhook message field, exposing authenticated phone-control tools
source_issues.evidence: aster forwards Android SMS/notification content to the agent webhook. Attacker who can send an SMS or notification to the victim's phone can embed injection text that steers the agent into unauthorized phone-control actions.

source_issues.title: Security: samj12/betbud-prediction-market-creation feeds raw trending crypto tweets into Claude prompt that drives Base Sepolia openNewMarket and betbud.live registration
source_issues.evidence: betbud-pm ingests raw crypto tweets and drives authenticated blockchain transactions (openNewMarket on Base Sepolia) and betbud.live registration. Attacker can tweet with injection text to trigger unauthorized market creation or account registration under the victim's blockchain identity.

source_issues.title: Security: robsannaa/shopify-admin ingests raw Shopify order and customer JSON into agent context, exposing authenticated Shopify Admin actions including delete-product
source_issues.evidence: shopify-admin ingests Shopify order/customer JSON with authenticated Shopify Admin mutations including delete-product. Attacker can send a crafted order with injection text in product/customer fields to steer the agent into unauthorized Shopify product deletions.

source_issues.title: Security: raunaksingwi/sunday ingests raw inbox email content into agent context, exposing E2E-encrypted credential vault commands (sunday passwords get/edit/delete)
source_issues.evidence: sunday ingests raw inbox email content and exposes authenticated credential vault commands (get/edit/delete passwords). Attacker who can send an email to the victim's inbox can embed injection text to trigger unauthorized vault credential retrieval or modification.

signals.topic: Unauthenticated MCP/SSE daemon exposes shell.exec and auto-registers agents, enabling remote code execution
signals.summary: rendis/opcode MCP/SSE daemon auto-registers agents and exposes built-in shell.exec on an unauthenticated endpoint, enabling any network attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the host.
signals.review_reason: Unauthenticated network service listening on all interfaces that exposes shell.exec to any caller is a concrete, direct remote code execution vector. Any user who installs opcode and runs 'opcode install --listen' (as SKILL.md instructs) exposes their host to arbitrary command execution by any network peer. No user interaction or multi-step exploitation chain required.

source_issues.title: Security: rendis/opcode exposes unauthenticated MCP/SSE endpoint on :4100 with auto-registered agents and built-in shell.exec, enabling remote code execution
source_issues.evidence: rendis/opcode MCP/SSE daemon installs via 'opcode install --listen' and binds to all interfaces without auth. The exposed endpoint auto-registers agents and exposes a built-in shell.exec tool callable by any network caller. Direct RCE vector: no user interaction, no credential, no confirmation required. Any local user or network peer who can reach :4100 gains OS command execution under the host user's authority.

signals.topic: Chat messages piped directly to subprocess shell=True, enabling chat-to-shell command execution
signals.summary: sadikjarvis/native-run bridges OpenClaw chat input directly to OS shell execution, bypassing all safety controls and allowing any chat message to trigger arbitrary shell commands.
signals.review_reason: Direct bridge from chat input to shell=True subprocess is a concrete RCE path requiring no multi-step chain. Any user with this plugin installed and the agent running can be exploited by an attacker sending specially crafted chat messages. The vulnerability bypasses all OpenClaw safety boundaries by design.

source_issues.title: Security: sadikjarvis/native-run forwards chat messages into subprocess shell=True on the local host, enabling chat-to-shell command execution
source_issues.evidence: sadikjarvis/native-run bridges OpenClaw chat input directly to subprocess shell=True on the local host. Any chat message accepted by the agent triggers shell command execution under the local user's authority. This bypasses all OpenClaw safety controls: the agent treats user text as natural language, but the plugin converts it to shell commands. Attackers can craft chat messages to execute arbitrary commands (file exfiltration, credential theft, persistence). No secondary exploitation chain needed.

signals.topic: Skill install events not reported to registry — installsAllTime and installsCurrent always show 0, breaking adoption metrics
signals.summary: The clawhub install command downloads skill files and writes local metadata but never POSTs an install event to the registry. The installsAllTime and installsCurrent counters are stuck at 0 for all skills, while downloads increment normally. Publishers cannot see real adoption, and marketplace sorting by installs is broken.
aliases: install event not reported to registry
signals.review_reason: Install event reporting is completely absent from the CLI-to-registry flow. The feature is broken for all skills and all users. Publishers cannot track adoption, the marketplace cannot surface popular skills via install counts, and the Convex schema field is permanently zeroed. This is a confirmed functional failure with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: installsAllTime / installsCurrent always 0 — install event not reported to registry
source_issues.evidence: API returns installsAllTime: 0 and installsCurrent: 0 for skills confirmed installed by multiple users. Root cause: clawhub install CLI downloads files and writes local metadata but has no HTTP POST to report install events to the registry. Publishers have no visibility into real adoption; marketplace install-based sorting is non-functional.

signals.topic: /api/v1/skills pagination cursor parameter has no effect — API always returns identical first page, blocking discovery beyond 10 results
signals.summary: GET /api/v1/skills never paginates. Every request returns the same first page of 10 results and the same nextCursor value regardless of the cursor parameter passed. Passing the server's own advertised nextCursor back yields a byte-identical response. This breaks all sorting modes (updated, createdAt, newest, downloads, installsAllTime, stars, trending). Users cannot browse beyond the first 10 skills.
aliases: skills API always returns first page
signals.review_reason: Pagination is a core API feature that is completely non-functional. Users cannot discover skills beyond the first page under any sort mode. The reproduction steps are byte-level verifiable and the bug is confirmed on the live service. This is a confirmed functional failure blocking the primary discovery workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Pagination not working on /api/v1/skills
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed with reproduction steps on clawhub.ai: passing the server's own nextCursor back yields byte-identical response. diff of r1.json and r2.json shows no difference. Same broken behavior across all tested sort modes. Users cannot access skills beyond the first page of 10 results.

signals.topic: MCP tools/list ships overly permissive inputSchema causing agent tool-call runtime failures
signals.summary: Every tool in MCP tools/list advertises { 'type': 'object', 'additionalProperties': true } with no per-parameter types, required fields, or enum constraints. Agents must infer parameter shapes from prose descriptions and receive InvalidOperationException at capability-execution time rather than upfront schema validation. This causes repeated tool-call failures and degraded cold-start for MCP-connected agents.
aliases: A2 MCP tool schema too broad
signals.review_reason: Agents using MCP integration repeatedly receive runtime validation errors instead of upfront schema errors. This is a recurring, reproducible failure pattern that directly degrades the AI-ergonomics core use case. Evidence is concrete: the permissive schema is explicitly documented in the issue body with the exact JSON shape and comparison to OpenAPI/MCP spec norms.

source_issues.title: [deep-review] A2: MCP tools/list ships permissive inputSchema for every tool
source_issues.evidence: inputSchema is { 'type': 'object', 'additionalProperties': true } for every tool; no type info, no required fields, no enums. Validation errors arrive from capability layer (e.g. 'maxWidth must be 16-4096') rather than schema layer, forcing agents to learn by trial and error.

source_issues.title: [deep-review] Tracking: 26 issues from senior-engineer multi-axis architecture review
source_issues.evidence: Tracks 26 findings; A2 (permissive MCP schema) is listed as a top-axis security/extensibility finding alongside 25 others.

signals.topic: system.execApprovals.set validator accepts arbitrary path Allow rules, bypassing command execution security policy
signals.summary: The execApprovals.set validator does not restrict the path patterns allowed in Allow rules. This means a user or automated process could configure overly permissive or intentionally malicious path allow-lists, undermining the purpose of the exec approval system. Combined with the V1 exec-wrapper detector not recognizing zsh/dash/ash/ksh/fish shells (D3), the policy evaluation surface is incomplete and inconsistent.
aliases: exec approval path allow-list too permissive
signals.review_reason: The exec approval system is a core security boundary controlling which commands can be executed. Accepting arbitrary path Allow rules defeats its purpose: a misconfigured or malicious rule can allow execution of any binary, bypassing the intended policy. This is a direct security control bypass with user impact — unintended commands can be executed.

source_issues.title: [deep-review] C7: system.execApprovals.set validator accepts arbitrary path Allow rules
source_issues.evidence: Validator accepts arbitrary path Allow rules without restriction. The exec approval system is designed to gate dangerous commands; permissive path allow-lists defeat this control entirely.

source_issues.title: [deep-review] Tracking: 26 issues from senior-engineer multi-axis architecture review
source_issues.evidence: C7 (arbitrary path Allow rules in execApprovals.set) is listed as a Critical/High-priority bug (C7 of 12) in the tracked findings.

signals.topic: WindowsNodeClient single-threaded receive loop lacks back-pressure, causing head-of-line blocking for concurrent messages
signals.summary: WebSocketClientBase.ListenForMessagesAsync calls ProcessMessageAsync sequentially. For WindowsNodeClient, a slow capability (screen.record, system.run, stt.transcribe) blocks all other inbound messages on the same connection, including health pings, pair events, and other invokes. This causes session timeouts, stalled auto-pair flows, and inability to cancel long-running operations.
aliases: slow capability blocks all concurrent WS messages
signals.review_reason: Users running any slow capability (screen.record, system.run, stt.transcribe) experience complete unresponsiveness for all other concurrent messages on the same session. The gateway may tear down the session due to missed health pings, auto-pair stalls, and cancel commands cannot get through. Concrete mechanism (sequential await with no back-pressure) and practical consequences (health ping loss, cancel blockage, pair stall) are explicitly described.

source_issues.title: [deep-review] A10: WindowsNodeClient single-threaded receive loop has no back-pressure (head-of-line blocking)
source_issues.evidence: Sequential await in ListenForMessagesAsync blocks health pings (gateway may drop session), blocks user-initiated cancel commands during screen.record, and stalls auto-pair events during stt.transcribe. Contrast: McpHttpServer uses SemaphoreSlim(16) with 503 fallback — same pattern absent in WindowsNodeClient.

signals.topic: Gateway unusable on Windows 10 after upgrade to 2026.5.12 — protocol mismatch blocks all access
signals.summary: After upgrading to 2026.5.12, the gateway reports 'protocol mismatch' on Windows 10. The browser shows 'Unauthorized' even for local 127.0.0.1 access, making the gateway completely unusable.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：升级后 gateway 在 Windows 10 上完全不可用，协议不匹配且认证失败，用户无法访问任何功能。此类阻断性 bug 在 count=1 的情况下仍应标记 P0，因为其影响覆盖整个平台的一个主要操作系统，且有明确的重现步骤和用户环境描述。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Gateway unusable on Windows 10: Protocol mismatch -> unauthorized
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading OpenClaw to 2026.5.12, gateway reports protocol mismatch on Windows 10. Browser redirected to 127.0.0.1:18791 shows 'Unauthorized'. Log shows 'protocol mismatch' and all models time out. All gateway use is blocked.

signals.topic: Gateway startup crash loop when brave search provider is configured (2026.5.12 regression)
signals.summary: Gateway pre-startup config validation checks provider availability before external plugins are loaded, causing an immediate crash loop when brave search is configured even though the brave plugin is correctly installed.
aliases: gateway fail to start with brave
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：gateway 完全无法启动（crash loop），用户配置了正确的 brave 插件但因验证时序错误导致 gateway 不可用。即使是 count=1 的单仓问题，强用户影响证据（明确的 startup failure + 可复现步骤）足以支撑 P0。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Gateway startup validation rejects tools.web.search.provider: "brave" even when brave plugin is correctly installed (2026.5.12)
source_issues.evidence: Gateway pre-startup config validation checks provider availability BEFORE external plugins are loaded. Brave was externalized from core in 2026.5.x so it is never available at validation time, causing immediate startup failure. Crash loop on every gateway start.

signals.topic: v2026.5.12 isolated ingress event-loop stall 14–194 seconds on every startup and first inbound message
signals.summary: A regression introduced in 2026.5.12 causes the event loop to block for 14–194 seconds during channels.telegram.start-account on every cold start and on the first inbound message. The Telegram getMe fetch times out and cascades failures.
signals.review_reason: 主流程严重降级：gateway 每次冷启动和第一个消息都会 stall 14-194 秒，极大影响用户体验和生产可用性。明确的主流程阻断（启动 + 首次收消息），且 2026.5.7 无此问题，是 2026.5.12 的明确回归。强证据支撑 P0。

source_issues.title: v2026.5.12 regression: isolated ingress startup blocks event loop 14-194s during channels.telegram.start-account
source_issues.evidence: Gateway hangs for 14-194 seconds on every cold start and on the first inbound message. The stall is in channels.telegram.start-account — the new isolated-ingress feature awaits pollingSession.runUntilAbort() sequentially per account. When event loop is already loaded, Telegram getMe fetch times out and cascades. Previous version 2026.5.7 had no such problem.

signals.topic: OpenRouter passthrough writes literal field-name string to thinkingSignature, breaking 2nd turn on reasoning models
signals.summary: On OpenRouter with reasoning models, the 1st turn succeeds but the 2nd turn is rejected by OpenRouter with HTTP 500 because a literal placeholder string (the OpenRouter response field name) is persisted as thinkingSignature instead of its value.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：多轮对话在第二回合被 OpenRouter 拒绝（HTTP 500），导致 reasoning 模型完全无法正常工作。这是明确的主流程失败，与之前 Anthropic/Bedrock signature poisoning 是同类问题，有直接的用户影响证据。

source_issues.title: OpenRouter passthrough: literal field-name string written to thinkingSignature, breaks 2nd turn on reasoning models (Anthropic, xAI)
source_issues.evidence: First turn succeeds but second turn is rejected by OpenRouter with HTTP 500. The malformed signature is replayed in history. This is analogous to previous Anthropic/Bedrock signature poisoning bugs. OpenRouter passthrough path (api: openai-completions, provider: openrouter) is affected.

signals.topic: Email delivery-recovery fires before startAccount completes on gateway startup (startup race)
signals.summary: The delivery-recovery system retries queued email deliveries within milliseconds of the HTTP server listening, before startAccount finishes auth and initialization (400-900ms), causing 'no runtime services registered' errors and failed retries.
aliases: email service not ready on startup
signals.review_reason: 体验下降 + 隐性数据损失：邮件投递系统在 gateway 启动时触发竞态条件，导致本应成功的邮件投递进入无限重试队列。关键邮件可能延迟或丢失，是明确的功能受损证据。

source_issues.title: email: delivery-recovery fires before startAccount/setServices completes on gateway startup (startup race)
source_issues.evidence: delivery-recovery retries within milliseconds of HTTP server listening, but startAccount takes 400-900ms to complete auth. Any queued email delivery during this window hits 'no runtime services registered' and records another failed retry. Pattern repeats on every startup.

signals.topic: WhatsApp Dispatch 显示已连接但不处理/回复消息（Windows）
signals.summary: 用户配置 WhatsApp Dispatch 并确认连接状态为绿色后，发送消息到 Self-chat，消息被标记为已读（蓝色双勾），但 Open Interpreter 桌面端完全无响应，主界面停留在 'What would you like to work on?' 界面，无任何代码执行或回复发送。
aliases: WhatsApp Dispatch message processing failure on Windows
WhatsApp integration not responding despite connected status
signals.review_reason: WhatsApp Dispatch 是 Open Interpreter 的关键集成功能（issue 标题明确使用 'bug' 标签），用户完成配置并确认连接后，主流程完全不工作：消息被 WhatsApp Web 读取（蓝色双勾）但数据未传递给 LLM 执行，也无任何回复发送。这属于关键功能不可用（key feature unavailable），且在 Windows 平台上明确可复现。虽然只有 1 条 issue，但用户提供了完整复现步骤、截图和环境信息，证据充分，因此标记为用户痛点。

source_issues.title: WhatsApp Dispatch connected but not processing or sending messages windows
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确复现步骤：WhatsApp Dispatch 连接后，发送 'Hi' 或 'ls' 到 Self-chat，消息在手机上显示已读（蓝色双勾），但 Open Interpreter 桌面 UI 没有任何反应，停留在 'What would you like to work on?' 界面。状态显示为 'Connected'，但 bridge between WhatsApp Web instance and interpreter core is broken。环境：Windows 11, Full Auto approval policy, LM Studio local model。

signals.topic: Repomap crashes with uncaught tree-sitter QueryError when parsing Python source files with certain AST node types
signals.summary: When generating the repo map, aider uses tree-sitter to parse Python files and runs AST queries. On certain Python source files, tree-sitter raises a QueryError with 'Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module', which is uncaught and crashes the entire application before any user task can begin.
aliases: repo map generation crashes on specific Python files
signals.review_reason: This is a high-frequency (3 issues in ~5 days), high-severity crash that completely blocks the main workflow. The crash occurs during repo-map generation, which is a mandatory early step in every aider session. Users cannot use aider at all when encountering this bug. The same root cause (tree-sitter QueryError on Python AST queries) manifests identically across three independent reports from three different OS platforms, confirming a systemic issue.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Crash occurs at app startup when generating repo map. Stack trace: repomap.py:302 raises tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module. Affects both Linux and macOS platforms.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Same crash on macOS. Confirms the issue is reproducible on different platforms with the same tree-sitter query parsing failure.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Same crash on Windows. Multiple users hit this independently across different OSes, confirming it is a systemic bug, not an edge case.

signals.topic: CLI argument values exceeding OS limit cause uncaught OSError (errno 63) and prevent app from starting
signals.summary: When system prompt or custom instruction values are passed via CLI arguments and exceed the OS argument length limit (ARG_MAX), the app crashes with an uncaught OSError at pathlib.is_dir() because the long string is incorrectly treated as a file path. The crash is a complete startup block.
aliases: long system prompt crashes aider on startup
OSError errno 63 from command line argument overflow
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports demonstrate this is a systemic issue, not an edge case. When users configure long system prompts or custom instructions via CLI arguments, the app crashes unconditionally at startup before any task can proceed. The app misinterprets the long argument string as a file path and attempts os.stat() on it, triggering errno 63. This is a complete user-blocking crash that affects anyone using substantial custom instructions via CLI.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 1222
source_issues.evidence: Full system prompt passed via --system-prompt exceeds OS limit. OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long. macOS Darwin 25.4.0, Python 3.9.6. The error occurs in Path(all_files[0]).is_dir() treating the long string as a path.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: Long --system-prompt-prefix causes the same crash. macOS Darwin 24.6.0, Python 3.12. Confirmed as the same root cause: argument value too long for OS.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: Long --custom-instruction causes the same crash. macOS Darwin 25.4.0, Python 3.12. Different CLI flags, same OS errno 63 root cause.

signals.topic: Benchmark tool uses --read-model-settings flag inconsistent with main CLI --model-settings-file, causing silent config load failure and hour-long hangs
signals.summary: The benchmark.py script uses --read-model-settings but the main CLI and official documentation reference --model-settings-file. Users following docs get no error, just silent config loading failure. For Qwen-family AWQ models this causes indefinite hangs as required tokens (min_p/top_p) are absent.
aliases: benchmark silent config load failure due to wrong flag name
signals.review_reason: This is a significant user experience failure with a large cost impact. Users following official documentation get zero error feedback — the config simply doesn't load. For specific model families (Qwen AWQ), the consequence is a silent multi-hour hang because required token parameters are absent. The user explicitly describes spending 'a couple of hours' debugging before finding the root cause. This qualifies as both a UX degradation and a cost/time loss, meeting the P1 threshold despite being a single report.

source_issues.title: benchmark.py uses `--read-model-settings` but main cli + docs say `--model-settings-file`
source_issues.evidence: User spent hours debugging a polyglot benchmark setup against a local vLLM endpoint. The benchmark silently loads no settings when --model-settings-file is used (because the flag is actually --read-model-settings in benchmark.py). For Qwen AWQ models, missing min_p/top_p tokens from the YAML causes indefinite long-decode hangs. The benchmark sets LONG_TIMEOUT = 24 hours, so the failure mode is a silent multi-hour hang. The user also notes the benchmark README correctly names the flag but links to docs that use the wrong name throughout.

signals.topic: aiohttp import on Windows throws AttributeError due to API incompatibility, preventing aider from starting
signals.summary: On Windows, importing litellm triggers a chain of imports that causes aiohttp to be loaded. Due to a version/API incompatibility, aiohttp does not expose ConnectionTimeoutError as an attribute, causing AttributeError at import time. Aider fails to start entirely on affected Windows environments.
aliases: Windows startup crash due to aiohttp import error
signals.review_reason: This is a complete startup block on Windows. The crash occurs during module initialization before aider's main function even begins, making the tool completely unusable for affected Windows users. While count=1, the nature of the crash (full app unavailability) combined with Windows being a primary platform justifies P1 rather than P2. The issue was closed with resolution, indicating the maintainers acknowledged and fixed it.

source_issues.title: Uncaught AttributeError in __init__.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: Windows 10, Python 3.11.4. The crash occurs at import time: aiohttp.__init__.py line 240 raises AttributeError: module aiohttp has no attribute ConnectionTimeoutError. This prevents litellm from loading, which blocks aider startup entirely. The issue was closed with a comment, suggesting a fix was applied, but the uncaught exception behavior represents a real crash users experienced.

signals.topic: Windows console UnicodeEncodeError crashes aider when output contains invalid UTF-8 surrogate characters
signals.summary: On Windows, when the Rich console encounters output with invalid UTF-8 surrogate characters (e.g., from certain LLM responses or special characters), it raises an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError at console.py line 2097. The crash terminates the session mid-workflow.
aliases: Windows UTF-8 surrogate crash in console
Rich console UnicodeEncodeError on Windows with special characters
signals.review_reason: This is a mid-workflow crash that terminates the session when encountering special characters on Windows. The crash cascades through error handlers and cannot be recovered from, causing complete session loss. While affecting only a subset of Windows users encountering specific character types, it is a real uncaught exception that breaks the main use case. Count=1 limits it to P2, but it should be tracked as a known Windows-specific encoding issue.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in console.py line 2097
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11, Python 3.12. Rich console crashes with UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 2828-2829: surrogates not allowed. The error occurs during output rendering, which is a core workflow step. The crash cascades through error handlers, ultimately terminating the entire application. PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 is suggested as a workaround but the app itself should handle this gracefully.

signals.topic: rag-poisoning plugin fails with 'Unknown grader' error during redteam evaluation, blocking all RAG poisoning tests
signals.summary: The rag-poisoning redteam plugin generates test assertions with type `promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning`, but no corresponding grader is registered in `src/redteam/graders.ts`. This causes 100% evaluation failure with `Invariant failed: Unknown grader` error for every generated test case.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow blocking bug for the rag-poisoning redteam plugin. The plugin generates assertions that cannot be evaluated because the corresponding grader is not registered. All generated test cases fail with a hard error — 0 passed, 2 errors (100%). Users cannot run RAG poisoning red team tests at all without manual workarounds. Count=1 because only one issue is present in this dataset, but the impact is severe and unambiguous.

source_issues.title: Bug: `rag-poisoning` tests fail during evaluation with `Unknown grader`
source_issues.evidence: 100% of generated rag-poisoning tests fail with 'Invariant failed: Unknown grader: promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning'. Test generation succeeds (2 test cases written to redteam.yaml) but evaluation fails for all cases. The error is reproducible with both echo target and real HTTP targets. Workaround requires manually replacing the generated assertion with llm-rubric.

signals.topic: Homebrew-installed esbuild fails to find @esbuild/darwin-arm64 binary on macOS ARM64, blocking code-scans run
signals.summary: When promptfoo is installed via Homebrew on macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon), esbuild cannot locate the @esbuild/darwin-arm64 native binary, throwing a TransformError. This blocks the `promptfoo code-scans run` command entirely.
aliases: code-scans run fails esbuild on macOS ARM64
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash that blocks the `code-scans run` command on macOS ARM64 via Homebrew installation. The esbuild binary is a critical dependency for promptfoo's transform pipeline. The error is a hard crash that prevents any code scanning workflow from running on this platform/configuration. Count=1 but the blocking nature is clear from the stack trace and the command that fails.

source_issues.title: The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found
source_issues.evidence: Homebrew installation on macOS ARM64 (win32/NUC environment) throws 'Error [TransformError]: The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found, and is needed by esbuild' when running `promptfoo code-scans run`. The error occurs in esbuild's generateBinPath function. The issue is confirmed on promptfoo 0.121.11 with Node.js v24.15.0.

signals.topic: undici v7 upgrade breaks HTTP responses with Content-Encoding gzip/brotli compression due to missing decompress interceptor on custom Agent
signals.summary: After upgrading to undici v7 (shipped in 0.121.x), the custom undici Agent used for connection pooling lacks the decompress interceptor. Compressed responses (gzip/Brotli) from remote APIs are returned as raw bytes, causing 'Unexpected token' JSON parse errors on every test against affected endpoints. Particularly impacts OpenAI API responses and web-search-enabled evaluations.
aliases: JSON parse error binary garbage compressed responses
content-encoding brotli gzip breaks API evaluations
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-breaking regression introduced by the undici v7 upgrade. The bug causes all evaluations against any provider returning gzip/brotli-compressed responses to fail with JSON parse errors containing binary garbage. The scope is broad: all OpenAI API calls and web-search-enabled evaluations are affected. The root cause is clearly identified (missing decompress interceptor on custom Agent), and the impact is systematic — every compressed response fails. Count=1 in this dataset but the bug has broad user impact across multiple provider types.

source_issues.title: fetch() with custom undici Agent does not decompress Content-Encoding responses (Brotli/gzip → garbage)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: undici v7 moved decompression from default Agent behavior to an opt-in interceptor. The custom Agent in getOrCreateAgent does not install the decompress interceptor, causing raw compressed bytes to be returned instead of decoded JSON. Every test against OpenAI API endpoints (especially /v1/responses and web-search-enabled evals) fails with 'Unexpected token <x>, <binary> is not valid JSON'. The bug is confirmed reproducible on 0.121.9 and 0.121.11 with undici 7.25.0 and Node.js v26.0.0/v24.x. Workaround: add 'Accept-Encoding: identity' per-provider.

signals.topic: SimpleChatEngine astream_chat crashes with ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks
signals.summary: When using SimpleChatEngine with streamed responses, consuming get_full_response() causes a ValueError crash because awrite_response_to_history() assigns to ChatMessage.content directly, but the message contains multiple blocks which is unsupported by the content setter. This blocks the main streaming chat flow.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking crash: the streaming chat engine crashes during response consumption, which is a core user workflow. The error is reproducible with a full stack trace, and it occurs when a user tries to get the final response from a streamed chat — completely blocking the feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks in SimpleChatEngine
source_issues.evidence: Crashes when calling get_full_response() on a streamed chat. Traceback shows ValueError: 'ChatMessage contains multiple blocks, use ChatMessage.blocks instead' raised from awrite_response_to_history() setting .content directly on a multi-block message.

signals.topic: GoogleGenAIEmbedding batch embedding returns single aggregated result instead of per-text embeddings with SDK v1.71.0+
signals.summary: When using google-genai SDK v1.71.0+ with gemini-embedding-2, get_text_embedding_batch returns a single aggregated embedding instead of one per input text, breaking all batch embedding workflows.
signals.review_reason: This breaks a core embedding feature: batch embedding returns wrong-length results silently, corrupting downstream RAG pipelines. The bug is directly demonstrated with expected vs actual output length.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: GoogleGenAIEmbedding with gemini-embedding-2 produces aggregated embeddings instead of individual ones with google-genai SDK v1.71.0+
source_issues.evidence: get_text_embedding_batch(['Hello', 'World']) returns list of length 1 instead of 2. Breaks batch embedding of documents in RAG pipelines. The SDK changed behavior in v1.71.0 without LlamaIndex adapting.

signals.topic: Async rate limiter (TokenBucketRateLimiter/SlidingWindowRateLimiter) uses blocking threading.Lock inside async methods, freezing the asyncio event loop
signals.summary: Both async_acquire() methods use threading.Lock which is a blocking OS syscall. When called from the asyncio event loop thread, it blocks all other coroutines for the lock duration. Under high concurrency this causes massive latency spikes and throughput collapse in async LLM/embedding pipelines.
aliases: asyncio event loop blocked by threading.Lock in rate limiter
signals.review_reason: Critical performance defect in async LLM/embedding pipelines: threading.Lock blocks the entire asyncio event loop, freezing all concurrent coroutines for up to 341ms per event. Any async pipeline using rate limiting is severely impacted. Complete blockage of concurrent async operations is a high-severity user impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: async_acquire() in TokenBucketRateLimiter and SlidingWindowRateLimiter blocks the asyncio event loop (threading.Lock used in async context)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows heartbeat coroutine frozen for 0.341s when 500 concurrent async_acquire() calls run. Max block duration: 0.341s, which is catastrophic for async pipelines. threading.Lock used instead of asyncio.Lock.

signals.topic: Pymilvus 2.6.4 breaks AsyncMilvusClient in MilvusVectorStore with RuntimeError: no running event loop
signals.summary: Using MilvusVectorStore with pymilvus 2.6.4 causes RuntimeError at initialization due to AsyncMilvusClient trying to get a running event loop outside an async context, blocking vector store usage entirely.
aliases: Milvus async vector store initialization failure
signals.review_reason: Async MilvusVectorStore is completely blocked with pymilvus 2.6.4: the vector store fails to initialize at runtime, preventing any async vector operations. This is a breaking change in a downstream dependency that LlamaIndex must handle or document a workaround for.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Pymilvus 2.6.4 breaks AsyncMilvusClient in MilvusVectorStore
source_issues.evidence: MilvusVectorStore.__init__ calls AsyncMilvusClient which calls asyncio.get_running_loop() at init time, outside any async context, raising RuntimeError. The issue is confirmed reproducible by installing pymilvus 2.6.4. Workaround: downgrade to 2.6.3.

signals.topic: RetryGuidelineQueryEngine causes ~400k token prompts when used with NLSQLTableQueryEngine synthesize_response=False, triggering massive cost and rate limit issues
signals.summary: When GuidelineEvaluator wraps NLSQLTableQueryEngine with synthesize_response=False, retry attempts send the entire raw database result set (thousands of rows) to the LLM as context, causing ~400k token prompts instead of just the generated SQL query. This leads to extreme cost and immediate rate limit hits.
signals.review_reason: This causes severe cost overruns (20x expected tokens) and immediate rate limit hits when using SQL guideline validation — a real financial impact for users. The feature works correctly without the wrapper, making this a clear regression.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: RetryGuidelineQueryEngine/GuidelineEvaluator causes ~400k token prompts when used with NLSQLTableQueryEngine(synthesize_response=False)
source_issues.evidence: User reports ~400k tokens in retry rewrite LLM calls instead of expected ~20k. The entire raw database result set is being passed to the LLM for evaluation when only the SQL query should be. Causes immediate rate limit hits and massive cost overruns.

signals.topic: semantic memory search 完全失效：默认安装 schema 为 768-dim 但模型输出 384-dim 向量
signals.summary: ruflo init --full --with-embeddings 后，memory search 永远返回 0 结果。根因是 schema.sql 硬编码 dimensions=768，但默认 ONNX 模型 (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) 输出 384-dim 向量，HNSW 拒绝索引 dimension 不匹配的向量。三个 bug 叠加：schema 写死 768-dim、index build 默认建在 wrong namespace、--threshold 默认 0.7 对短查询语义相似度太高。
signals.review_reason: 核心功能在默认安装路径下完全失效，影响所有平台所有用户。语义搜索是 ruflo 的 headline feature，clean install 后永远返回 0 结果，用户会直接认为该功能已损坏。repro 路径完整，根因（dimension mismatch）有 hex 对比证据。

source_issues.title: memory search returns 0 results on default install: schema is 768-dim but default model is 384-dim
source_issues.evidence: schema.sql 硬编码 dimensions=768，但默认模型 all-MiniLM-L6-v2 输出 384-dim 向量，HNSW 拒绝索引；三个叠加 bug：schema、namespace、threshold 均不正确；repro 覆盖完整 store→search 链路，返回 0 结果；用户反馈：'headline feature is broken on default install'

signals.topic: npm 安装失败：alpha 版本因 transitive dep @huggingface/transformers 导致 Invalid Version 错误
signals.summary: @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38 (tagged latest/alpha) 通过 npx 安装时失败，报 npm error Invalid Version: (空版本字符串)。根因是 @claude-flow/embeddings@3.0.0-alpha.15 的 transitive dep @huggingface/transformers 的 manifest version 字段为空，导致 npm arborist dedupe 步骤崩溃。这是历史性 recurring pattern 的新变体（历史 @xenova/transformers，见 #858/#1147）。
signals.review_reason: 主安装路径阻断：npx @claude-flow/cli@latest 对所有最新环境 (npm 11.x/Node 24+) 失败。doctor/status/MCP server 均无法通过默认安装路径使用。且为 recurring pattern，同类问题历史上已出现多次（第3次），说明修复不彻底。

source_issues.title: @claude-flow/cli@3.7.0-alpha.38 fails with npm 'Invalid Version' (regression of #1147 pattern)
source_issues.evidence: npx @claude-flow/cli@latest doctor 失败，npm error Invalid Version:；错误堆栈定位到 arborist pruneDedupable 读取空 version 字段；提供了完整 repro 步骤和 workaround（回退到 alpha.37）；作者明确标注为 #1147 pattern 的 regression；影响所有 npm 11.x / Node 24+ 用户

signals.topic: Windows 内存操作全面失效：memory store/search/stats 均无法正常工作
signals.summary: 在 Windows 11 + ruflo v3.7.0-alpha.27 下，memory store 虽打印成功但 search 返回 No results found、stats 显示 Total Entries: 0。re-init 时触发 UV handle assertion failed (UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)。与 Linux/macOS 共享相同代码但行为不同，表明存在平台特定的文件系统或 SQLite 句柄处理差异。
aliases: Windows memory store succeeds but search returns no results
UV handle assertion failed on Windows
signals.review_reason: Windows 用户完整内存工作流失效（store/search/stats 均不可用），且 re-init 时产生 assertion failed，触及 Node.js 底层 UV 层。在 Windows 市场份额显著的背景下，这是关键平台的功能阻断。注意 issue 1947（dimension mismatch）的 Windows 部分与本 issue 不同根因，前者影响所有平台。

source_issues.title: Windows: memory store succeeds but search returns no results and stats shows 0 entries (v3.7.0-alpha.27)
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 完整 repro 链路：init→store→search→stats，store 打印成功但 search 返回 No results found、stats 显示 0；re-init 触发 Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)；daemon logs 无 explicit memory errors 但操作无效

signals.topic: plugin-agent-federation 安装被 registry 403 阻断（cookies@0.9.1 via koa-router@14 transitive dep）
signals.summary: @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@alpha (1.0.0-alpha.15) 在 npm install 时因 transitive dep 链（koa-router@14 → cookies@0.9.1）被 registry 返回 403 Forbidden 而安装失败。koa-router@14 已 deprecated，其依赖的 cookies@0.9.1 在某些安全策略环境下被阻止。
signals.review_reason: plugin 安装管道完全失败，severity:high label，automated verification 持续监控发现。koa-router@14 deprecated 且其 dep 被 registry block，影响所有使用安全策略 registry 的用户。federation 功能完全不可用。

source_issues.title: [verification] HIGH — @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation@alpha install fails: 403 Forbidden on cookies@0.9.1 (koa-router transitive dep)
source_issues.evidence: 自动验证管道 12 小时检查发现：npm install federation@alpha 失败，E403 cookies@0.9.1；dep chain: federation→koa-router@14→cookies@0.9.1；koarouter@14 已被 upstream deprecated；label 含 severity:high；影响任何有安全策略阻止该包的环境

signals.topic: ruflo-browser session_record 工具失败（ruvector rvf create 缺少 --dimension flag），23 个下游 skill 全部阻断
signals.summary: ruflo-browser@0.2.0 的 MCP 工具 browser_session_record 调用 ruvector rvf create 时未传递必需的 -d, --dimension <n> 参数，导致每次调用都失败。23 个依赖 session 创建的 browser skill（login/record/test/extract/form-fill/auth-flow/replay/screenshot-diff 等）全部不可用，使整个 browser 自动化栈形同虚设。
aliases: ruvector rvf create required option not specified
signals.review_reason: plugin 核心 session 创建功能完全不可用，影响整个 browser skill 生态（23 tools）。bug 位置精确（wrapper 少传一个 flag），repro 简单明确。影响实际安全工作流（bug bounty workspace），有明确经济损失场景。

source_issues.title: ruflo-browser 0.2.0: browser_session_record fails — ruvector rvf create missing required -d, --dimension flag
source_issues.evidence: MCP tool 每次调用都失败，error: required option '-d, --dimension <n>' not specified；影响 23 个 browser skill（browser-login/test/record/extract/form-fill/auth-flow/replay/screenshot-diff 等）；作者因 browser-login workflow 无法进行 bug bounty 工作；提供了精确的 wrapper 代码行号和 fix 方向

signals.topic: Navigation reports success but returns stale/wrong content from prior browsing session
signals.summary: When the daemon is in a half-dead/recovered state (e.g., after a failed close), open commands report success (✓ Done) with the correct URL title, but content queries (snapshot, screenshot, get text body) return content from a completely different, previously-loaded page. This is silent data corruption that misleads AI agents into reading wrong content.
aliases: open reports success but content is stale
navigation false positive after daemon failure
session state doesn't reflect actual navigation
signals.review_reason: Two issues both involve the daemon reporting success while actual browser state is wrong/unresolved. #1367 is a main-flow data corruption issue where AI agents silently read wrong content — directly blocks reliable agentic browsing. #1365 blocks the --auto-connect feature entirely due to insufficient timeout. Both have clear, reproducible user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: After failed close, subsequent open reports success but returns stale content from prior URL
source_issues.evidence: open command shows ✓ correct page title, but screenshot/snapshot returns content from rustih.ru 404 page and other prior URLs. The '✓ Done' message lies. AI agent reads wrong literary work entirely.

source_issues.title: `--auto-connect` fails too quickly when Chrome asks for remote debugging permission
source_issues.evidence: --auto-connect times out after ~2 seconds before user can click Chrome's 'Allow' permission prompt. Feature is unusable for both manual and automated workflows requiring remote debugging permission approval.

signals.topic: Screencast consumers freeze when recording stops
signals.summary: Page.stopScreencast is unconditionally called when a record session stops, freezing all other screencast consumers (notably the built-in live-preview stream). Users see a frozen live preview after recording auto-stops or is explicitly stopped, until session close.
aliases: live preview freezes after recording stops
signals.review_reason: User describes frozen live preview as a direct consequence of the Page.stopScreencast call — a specific, reproducible failure mode. No refcounting means recording and live preview cannot coexist without the freeze. While count=1, the failure is well-understood and the fix is clearly scoped, making this actionable.

source_issues.title: fix(recording): Page.stopScreencast on record stop freezes other screencast consumers
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: spawn_recording_task unconditionally calls Page.stopScreencast with no refcount for consumers. Live preview stream stops receiving frames; daemon state.screencasting remains true; monitoring loop sleeps indefinitely. User impact: frozen live preview after recording auto-stops (5-min cap) or explicit stop.

signals.topic: network route --body mock response completely broken due to CLI parser / daemon handler field mismatch
signals.summary: The --body flag on `network route` has no effect because the CLI parser stores the value as a top-level 'body' field, but the daemon handler only reads from the nested 'response.body' path. All mock-based development workflows using --body are completely unusable.
aliases: network mock --body flag has no effect
Fetch.fulfillRequest never called due to data flow disconnect
signals.review_reason: This is a complete functional breakage of the `network route --body` feature — a core mock/intercept capability. The bug is precisely identified (field name mismatch between parser and handler) and is fully reproducible. Mock-based development workflows are entirely blocked.

source_issues.title: Bug: `network route --body` has no effect — CLI parser and handler field mismatch
source_issues.evidence: Root cause confirmed in code: parser stores body at cmd['body'], handler reads from cmd['response']['body']. Test shows --body returns real httpbin.org response instead of mocked. --abort works correctly as control group, proving CDP interception is fine. --body is entirely broken.

signals.topic: Proxy environment variables with trailing slash cause ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES and tool unusable
signals.summary: When HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY environment variables contain a trailing slash (common in systems configured via desktop GUIs or third-party tools like Clash, GNOME Settings), agent-browser open fails with net::ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES because Chromium's --proxy-server flag does not accept trailing slashes.
aliases: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES from trailing slash in proxy URL
proxy URL normalization missing trailing slash trim
signals.review_reason: Proxy configuration is a common enterprise/CI pattern. The failure is silent and confusing (ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES with no explanation), caused by a trailing slash that many popular proxy tools automatically add. Users cannot use agent-browser behind a proxy unless they manually sanitize environment variables — a non-obvious workaround.

source_issues.title: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES when proxy environment variables contain trailing slash
source_issues.evidence: Verified: HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7890/ fails with ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES; without trailing slash works. Root cause: chrome.rs directly passes proxy URL to --proxy-server without trimming trailing slash. Common scenario: desktop GUIs (Clash Verge, GNOME Settings, KDE) auto-add trailing slash, users unaware.

signals.topic: --ignore-https-errors flag silently ignored after daemon restart (regression of #372)
signals.summary: The --ignore-https-errors flag is silently ignored on all CLI invocations after the daemon is first started, even when the daemon was itself started with that flag and subsequent calls pass the same flag. This is a regression of fix #372 which covered --executable-path.
aliases: daemon flag mismatch warning floods stderr
signals.review_reason: While the reporter calls the impact 'cosmetic', the warning floods stderr on every command in projects requiring ignoreHttpsErrors (e.g., local dev with self-signed certs). This degrades the developer experience significantly and forces workaround wrapping of the CLI. A clear regression from a previously-fixed similar issue (#372 for --executable-path).

source_issues.title: --ignore-https-errors ignored: daemon already running (regression of #372)
source_issues.evidence: Warning '⚠ --ignore-https-errors ignored: daemon already running' printed on every CLI call. The daemon was started with the flag; subsequent calls also pass it but are told it's ignored. Users with self-signed certs must either drop the flag (breaking local dev) or wrap CLI with stderr filter. Affects versions 0.25.3 and 0.27.0.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock: tool-result content handling has three related bugs — image-url throws, PDF/file rejected, empty content causes API rejection
signals.summary: Three Bedrock tool-result conversion bugs: (1) image-url parts throw instead of auto-downloading, (2) PDFs/documents throw UnsupportedFunctionalityError, (3) step-start blocks with empty text produce content:[] which Bedrock rejects. Root cause is the tool-result branch in convertToBedrockChatMessages not mirroring the user-message branch.
aliases: bedrock tool result file content error
bedrock empty assistant content step-start rejection
signals.review_reason: Three related bugs with the same root cause (Bedrock tool-result branch in convertToBedrockChatMessages is incomplete vs the user-message branch). Combined count=3 with clear API rejection errors and blocked workflows. At least one issue (#15248) causes direct API failure, qualifying as P0. The other two block tool-result usage for PDFs and image URLs on Bedrock.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock] file content in tool results rejects PDFs and other documents
source_issues.evidence: UnsupportedFunctionalityError: 'media type: application/pdf' functionality not supported. Bedrock Converse API accepts 'document' as a ToolResultContentBlock member, but the tool-result branch only handles image types.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: image-url in tool-result throws instead of auto-downloading
source_issues.evidence: AI_UnsupportedFunctionalityError: 'unsupported tool content part type: image-url' functionality not supported. User-message URLs are auto-downloaded; tool-result URLs throw.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock sends empty assistant content for UIMessage step-start blocks
source_issues.evidence: convertToModelMessages produces empty text parts at step-start boundaries. Bedrock rejects 'The content field in the Message object at messages.N is empty' — API validation error.

signals.topic: Cerebras provider: structured output fails when combined with tools (finishReason becomes tool-call, triggering NoOutputGeneratedError)
signals.summary: When using Cerebras with both tools and structured output, the agent's finishReason is 'tool-calls' instead of 'stop', causing NoOutputGeneratedError at output access. Makes Cerebras + tools + structured output unusable.
signals.review_reason: A specific provider regression that renders the Cerebras + tools + structured output combination non-functional. While count=1 and single-repo, the impact is a main flow failure (NoOutputGeneratedError thrown), not a degraded experience. This is an agent-level use case that is completely blocked.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/cerebras] Cerebras does not work with tools + structured output
source_issues.evidence: finishReason is 'tool-calls' instead of 'stop' when using both tools and structured output, causing AI_NoOutputGeneratedError at runtime. No workaround within the SDK; users must parse result.text manually.

signals.topic: Baseten/GLM SSE reasoning_content chunks too small, causing UI stuttering
signals.summary: Baseten GLM models emit reasoning_content in tiny SSE chunks (1-2 words per event), causing visible UI stuttering during streaming. Requires users to implement custom buffering proxies.
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation for users of Baseten GLM thinking models — the streaming experience is visually broken. While not a crash or main flow block, the stuttering makes real-time thinking output unusable. The SDK has precedent (PR #14760 buffering for tool call deltas) for addressing this class of issue.

source_issues.title: Tiny SSE chunks from Baseten GLM models cause UI stuttering with reasoning_content
source_issues.evidence: Each reasoning token arrives as a separate SSE event (1-2 words). UI displays 'Thinking: 1. Report / Thinking: this as a bug / Thinking: to OpenCode...' instead of buffered output. User reports custom proxy buffering is required as workaround.

signals.topic: AI Gateway: previousResponseId fails silently for OpenAI Responses API across Vercel-managed pooled credentials
signals.summary: When using AI Gateway with Vercel-managed (non-BYOK) credentials, previousResponseId (conversation persistence) silently fails because Gateway load-balances across pooled OpenAI accounts — Responses IDs are account-scoped. Users see no error but lose multi-turn state.
aliases: gateway pooled credentials previousResponseId silent failure
AI Gateway conversation persistence pooled accounts
signals.review_reason: Silent state loss in multi-turn conversations — the most common production AI application pattern. previousResponseId round-trip appears to succeed but persistence is non-functional, leading to data loss without any error signal. count=1 but critical impact as this is a core API feature (OpenAI Responses API persistence) that fails silently for all Gateway users without BYOK configured.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: previousResponseId fails for OpenAI Responses API across pooled credentials
source_issues.evidence: Turn 1 returns valid resp_* id. Turn 2 reply: 'I don't have access to your name based on the current information...' — previousResponseId silently ignored. 5/5 model variants fail. BYOK per-request resolves it. Root cause: Gateway pools multiple OpenAI accounts, and Responses IDs are account-scoped, so sticky routing is required.

signals.topic: WorkflowAgent crashes with TypeError when passed non-string LanguageModel from openai provider (serialization bug)
signals.summary: WorkflowAgent (v7) crashes with 'TypeError: this.config.url is not a function' on first model call when given a LanguageModel object (e.g. openai('gpt-4o-mini')) instead of a string. Root cause: serializeModelOptions strips the url closure; deserialization never rebuilds it.
aliases: WorkflowAgent this.config.url is not a function serialization
signals.review_reason: Main flow crash for WorkflowAgent v7 (a core new feature) when using the most natural provider instantiation pattern (openai('model') as LanguageModel object). count=1 but blocks an entire product feature for all non-string model users across multiple providers.

source_issues.title: [v7] WorkflowAgent: this.config.url is not a function when using openai(...) as a non-string model
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: this.config.url is not a function at OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel.doStream. Affects all providers using url: ({ path }) => ... closure pattern including @ai-sdk/openai, @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, cerebras, deepinfra, deepseek, fireworks, groq, moonshotai, togetherai.

signals.topic: Vercel deployment fails with missing @swc/helpers module causing HTTP 500
signals.summary: Clean Next.js projects deployed to Vercel crash at runtime with 'Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js', causing MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED and FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED on production deploys.
signals.review_reason: Production deployment completely blocked on Vercel for clean projects. Two independent reports confirm the same failure mode. Root cause is module bundling/packaging mismatch in standalone artifact that causes @swc/helpers to be missing at runtime on Vercel serverless.

source_issues.title: MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED on Vercel deploy: Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js
source_issues.evidence: Cannot find module '/var/task/node_modules/@swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js'. HTTP 500 — MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED. A clean create-next-app@16.2.6 project with 3-line middleware fails on Vercel.

source_issues.title: MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED + FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED on Vercel deploy: Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report with same root cause. Production deployment completely blocked on Vercel.

signals.topic: Turbopack chunk filenames with multiple dots trigger WAF 403 blocking production loads
signals.summary: Turbopack generates chunk filenames like '0od.e4.nsryo4.js' (3+ dots) which standard WAF rules interpret as multiple file extension patterns and block with HTTP 403, causing ChunkLoadError in production behind reverse proxies/WAFs.
aliases: Turbopack chunk names trigger WAF blocking
signals.review_reason: Blocks entire production deployment when Turbopack is used and the app is behind standard WAF configurations. ChunkLoadError prevents any JS from executing. Two independent reports with minimal repro confirmed.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack generates chunk filenames with multiple dots (e.g., 0od.e4.nsryo4.js). WAF rules flag 'multiple file extension' patterns and return 403 Forbidden. Results in ChunkLoadError at runtime in production.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate confirming same root cause. Production chunk loading fails behind standard WAFs/reverse proxies.

signals.topic: IncrementalCache memory leak causes OOM in standalone mode production
signals.summary: Per-request IncrementalCache instances are retained by AsyncLocalStorage captured by Node keep-alive HTTPS sockets, causing linear heap growth until OOM in standalone deployments under sustained moderate traffic.
signals.review_reason: Causes production server OOM crashes in standalone mode, which is a primary Next.js deployment target. Heap snapshot evidence clearly shows linear growth. While single report, the severity (OOM crash) and the specific regression in a widely-used mode justify P0.

source_issues.title: Per-request IncrementalCache leaked via AsyncLocalStorage captured by keep-alive fetch sockets (15.5.18 standalone)
source_issues.evidence: Heap grows linearly with time. FileSystemCache and LRUNode counts grow monotonically. Per-request IncrementalCache objects retained by AsyncResource handles on live TLS sockets in keep-alive pool. Regression from 15.5.15 to 15.5.18. Verified with heap snapshots under sustained traffic.

signals.topic: Server-only pages crash with clientReferenceManifest undefined in production
signals.summary: Pages without client components don't generate clientReferenceManifest at runtime, causing 'Expected clientReferenceManifest to be defined' error and HTTP 500 on affected pages in production deployments.
signals.review_reason: Production-only regression causing HTTP 500 on server-only pages. Affects critical landing pages that may not have client components. Single but clear report with explicit error message and production impact.

source_issues.title: Bug: Runtime 500 - clientReferenceManifest undefined for server-only pages in Next.js 15.5.18
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'Expected clientReferenceManifest to be defined. This is a bug in Next.js.' Server-only pages (no client components) don't generate manifests. Production-only issue. Critical landing pages return 500.

signals.topic: Turbopack build emits missing chunks non-deterministically causing intermittent 500s in production
signals.summary: next build with Turbopack completes without errors but omits chunks referenced by page.js files, causing different routes to 500 at runtime with no build-time warning. Dangerous for CI/CD as builds can pass and still produce broken production deploys.
aliases: Turbopack missing chunks non-deterministic build failure
signals.review_reason: Produces silent production failures with no build-time indication. CI/CD pipelines pass and deploy broken code. Turbopack is the flagship build tool. Severity and scope (any route can be affected non-deterministically) justify P0 despite single report.

source_issues.title: next build (Turbopack) emits page.js with references to chunks that are missing on disk
source_issues.evidence: Build completes with no errors but .next/server/chunks/ssr/ is missing chunks that page.js files reference. Subsequent requests to different routes 500. Non-deterministic across rebuilds. Dangerous for CI/CD — builds pass but deploys produce 500 errors.

signals.topic: Task completion race: outputs not yet on disk when dependents start
signals.summary: When a task spawns subprocesses that detach from the process group (detached:true, setsid, double-fork), Turbo prematurely signals task completion as soon as the direct child exits, before declared outputs are written. Dependent tasks (^build-style) are scheduled immediately and fail with 'Could not resolve' / 'Cannot find module'. Affects real-world tools like `bunx --bun <cli>` and Prisma generators. In synthetic tests: 99.5-100% failure rate for detached/double-fork modes.
